questions.explanation: Meiosis is specifically called reductional division because it reduces the chromosome number by half, from diploid (2n) to haploid (n), producing gametes. Mitosis is equational division.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct order of the evolutionary history of man? a. Peking man, Neanderthal man, Homo sapiens, Heidelberg man b. Peking man, Homo sapiens, Neanderthal man, Cromagnon man c. Peking man, Heidelberg man, Neanderthal man, Cromagnon man d. Peking man, Lucy man, Neanderthal man, Cromagnon man

options.A: Peking man, Neanderthal man, Homo sapiens, Heidelberg man
options.B: Peking man, Homo sapiens, Neanderthal man, Cromagnon man
options.C: Peking man, Heidelberg man, Neanderthal man, Cromagnon man
options.D: Peking man, Lucy man, Neanderthal man, Cromagnon man

questions.explanation: The general chronological order of these hominins is: Peking man (Homo erectus, ~0.5-1 mya), Heidelberg man (Homo heidelbergensis, ~0.7-0.2 mya), Neanderthal man (Homo neanderthalensis, ~0.4-0.04 mya), and Cro-Magnon man (early Homo sapiens, ~0.05 mya).

questions.stem: For the seed shape trait, the dominant variant was __________ and the recessive was wrinkled.
questions.explanation: For the seed shape trait, the dominant variant was Round and the recessive was wrinkled.

questions.stem: In sequential hermaphroditism, which pattern describes individuals that begin life as females and later become males?
questions.explanation: Protogyny ('first female') is a form of sequential hermaphroditism where an organism is born female and later changes sex to male.

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules functions as both a base and a catalyst in cells?
questions.explanation: Certain RNA molecules, called ribozymes, can act as biological catalysts (like enzymes) and also serve as informational molecules (like mRNA). This dual function is a key piece of evidence for the 'RNA world' hypothesis.

questions.stem: Which hormone, released by the pituitary gland, contributes to uterine contractions during labor?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is released by the pituitary gland and contributes to producing uterine contractions during labor.

questions.stem: Sex cells are produced by what type of cell division?
questions.explanation: Sex cells (gametes: sperm and eggs) are produced by a specialized type of cell division called meiosis. Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half, producing haploid cells, and introduces genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment.

questions.stem: The physical expression of a trait is the _____ of the individual
questions.explanation: The phenotype is the set of observable characteristics or traits of an organism, such as its morphology, development, and behavior. It is the physical expression of the genotype.

questions.stem: Taxonomic hierarchy refers to: a. Step-wise arrangement of all categories for classification of plants and animals b. A group of senior taxonomists who decide the nomenclature c. A list of botanists d. Classification based on fossil record

options.A: Step-wise arrangement of all categories for classification of plants and animals
options.B: A group of senior taxonomists who decide the nomenclature

questions.explanation: Taxonomic hierarchy refers to the system of arranging taxonomic categories (ranks) in a descending order from the most broad (kingdom) to the most specific (species). It's a step-wise, nested system of classification.

questions.stem: Klinefelter's syndrome is XXY
questions.explanation: True. Klinefelter syndrome occurs in males who have an extra X chromosome, resulting in a karyotype of 47,XXY.

questions.stem: Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)

options.A: is secreted by females but not males
options.B: stimulates the seminiferous tubules to produce sperm
options.C: secretion is controlled by gonadotropic-releasing hormones (GnRH)
options.D: both B and C are correct

questions.explanation: FSH is secreted by the anterior pituitary in both males and females. In males, it acts on the seminiferous tubules to support spermatogenesis. Its secretion is stimulated by GnRH from the hypothalamus. Therefore, B and C are correct.

questions.stem: How many genotypes are produced by the 4 human blood groups: A, B, AB and O?
questions.explanation: The ABO blood group is determined by a single gene with three alleles: I^A, I^B, and i. I^A and I^B are codominant, and both are dominant over i. The possible genotypes are: I^A I^A, I^A i (both giving blood type A), I^B I^B, I^B i (both giving blood type B), I^A I^B (giving blood type AB), and i i (giving blood type O). That's a total of 6 distinct genotypes.

questions.stem: The cell division process restricted to the germplasm (or meiocytes) is: A. Cytokinesis B. Mitosis C. Karyokinesis D. Meiosis
questions.explanation: Meiosis is a specialized type of cell division that occurs only in germline cells (meiocytes) to produce gametes. Mitosis and its associated processes (karyokinesis, cytokinesis) occur in somatic cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following macromolecules contains the most energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Lipids (fats) store more energy per gram than carbohydrates or proteins because they have long hydrocarbon chains with many C-H bonds, which yield more energy when oxidized.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a property of all living organisms?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is a process carried out by autotrophs (plants, some algae, and bacteria) to produce their own food. Heterotrophs (animals, fungi, many bacteria) do not perform photosynthesis; they obtain energy by consuming other organisms. Reproduction, movement (at some level), and respiration (cellular) are properties shared by all living things.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes all the living organisms in a particular ecosystem? a. Community b. Sub-ecosystem c. Minor ecosystem d. Family
questions.explanation: The term 'community' specifically refers to all the living organisms (biotic components) present and interacting in an ecosystem.

questions.stem: Photosystem 2 occurs before photosystem 1
questions.explanation: True. In the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis, electrons flow through Photosystem II first, then through Photosystem I. They were numbered in order of discovery, not in the order they function.

questions.stem: _________ & _________ concluded that all plants & all animals were made of cells respectively
questions.explanation: In 1838-39, Matthias Schleiden (a botanist) concluded that all plants are composed of cells. Theodor Schwann (a zoologist) extended this idea to animals, concluding that all animal tissues are also composed of cells. Together, they formally proposed the cell theory.

questions.stem: In taxonomy, each level of classification is referred to as the:
questions.explanation: Each level of classification (e.g., genus, family) is a taxon.

questions.stem: When a particular gene is said to be 'sex-linked' on which chromosome is that gene usually present?
questions.explanation: Sex-linked traits are typically associated with genes located on the X chromosome. This is because the X chromosome carries many more genes than the Y chromosome. Traits on the Y chromosome are called Y-linked or holandric.

questions.stem: The mitochondrial genome encodes proteins primarily related to:
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes a small number of proteins, most of which are hydrophobic subunits of the electron transport chain complexes (like parts of Complex I, III, IV, and ATP synthase).

questions.stem: On tRNA, the __________ complements the mRNA codon.
questions.explanation: On tRNA, the anticodon complements the mRNA codon.

questions.stem: The breeding of plants and animals for particular traits by humans is called: a. paleontology b. artificial selection c. sexual recombination d. natural selection
questions.explanation: When humans, rather than the natural environment, choose which organisms to breed based on desired traits, it's called artificial selection (or selective breeding). This process has produced the wide variety of domesticated plants and animals.

questions.stem: For the height trait, the genotypes can be TT, Tt, or __________.
questions.explanation: For the height trait, the genotypes can be TT, Tt, or tt.

questions.stem: The primary function is to regulate metabolism, growth, and __________.
questions.explanation: By controlling DNA replication and gene expression, the nucleus directs cellular activities, including preparation for and execution of cell division.

questions.stem: TDF promotes development of the __________ phenotype.
questions.explanation: Expression of TDF initiates a cascade leading to testis formation and male characteristics.

questions.stem: Structures that may help in the conversion of lipids to carbohydrates are
questions.explanation: Glyoxysomes are specialized peroxisomes found in the fat-storing tissues of germinating plant seeds. They contain enzymes that convert stored lipids into carbohydrates via the glyoxylate cycle, providing energy for the growing seedling.

questions.stem: Similarities are greatest between the individuals in a:
questions.explanation: In biological classification (taxonomy), the hierarchy from broadest to most specific is: Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Similarities increase as you move down the hierarchy. Therefore, individuals in the same genus are more similar than those in the same family, order, or class. Species is not listed, but genus is the most specific among the options.

questions.stem: In scientific enquiry, which of the following is tested? a. a theory b. a result c. a hypothesis d. a prediction
questions.explanation: In the scientific method, a hypothesis is a testable explanation or prediction. Experiments and observations are designed to test the validity of a hypothesis. A theory is a well-tested, broad explanation.

questions.stem: The plantain reproduces asexually by: a. Suckers b. Buds c. Fragments d. Spores
questions.explanation: Plantain (a type of banana plant) reproduces asexually through underground stems called suckers. These suckers grow from the base of the parent plant and develop into new plants.

questions.stem: Which of these connotes a hybrid?
questions.explanation: The 'x' in 'Cistus x purpureus' indicates a hybrid.

questions.stem: What is capacitation in the context of sperm physiology?

options.B: Biochemical changes enabling sperm to fertilize an egg

questions.explanation: Capacitation is a final maturation process that sperm undergo within the female reproductive tract. It involves changes to the sperm membrane that enable the acrosomal reaction and hyperactive motility.

questions.stem: Living things show __________, meaning the environment influences survival.
questions.explanation: Living things show adaptation, meaning the environment influences survival.

questions.stem: At 20 days after fertilization, what is the size of the embryo?
questions.explanation: Twenty days after fertilization, the embryo is about 1.5 cm in size.

questions.stem: The cell theory was proposed in: A. 1839 B. 1836 C. 1590 D. 1665
questions.explanation: The formal proposal of the Cell Theory, based on the combined work of Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann, is generally dated to 1839. Schwann's book 'Microscopic Investigations on the Accordance in the Structure and Growth of Plants and Animals' was published that year.

questions.stem: The branch of biology that studies interactions between organisms and their environment is __________.
questions.explanation: The branch of biology that studies interactions between organisms and their environment is ecology.

questions.stem: An egg that has been fertilized by a sperm is called a: a. fetus b. zygote c. embryo d. gamete
questions.explanation: A fertilized egg is called a zygote. It is the single-celled stage resulting from the fusion of the male and female gametes. The zygote then undergoes cleavage to form an embryo.

questions.stem: Chromosomes uncoil to form __________.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes decondense back into loose chromatin, allowing gene expression to resume.

questions.stem: The start codon codes for the amino acid __________.
questions.explanation: The start codon (AUG) codes for the amino acid Methionine (Met).

questions.stem: In Kreb's cycle, a six carbon compound is formed by the combination of Acetyl CoA and
questions.explanation: The Krebs cycle begins when the two-carbon acetyl group from acetyl CoA combines with the four-carbon oxaloacetic acid (OAA) to form the six-carbon molecule citric acid (citrate).

questions.stem: The monomers for carbohydrates are __________.
questions.explanation: The monomers for carbohydrates are monosaccharides.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental difference between plant and animal cells?

options.D: Presence of a cell wall in plant cells

questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall external to the plasma membrane, composed primarily of cellulose. Animal cells lack a cell wall.

questions.stem: They maintain an acidic internal pH of about __________.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes maintain a pH around 5.0 via proton pumps. This acidic environment is optimal for hydrolytic enzymes and prevents damage if they leak.

questions.stem: A system of ducts and chambers, which receive and carry gametes and house the embryo and fetus is the: a. Cervix, Vagina, ovaries and Fallopian tube b. Cervix and Uterus c. Fallopian tube and gametes d. Vagina, ovaries and Uterus

options.A: Cervix, Vagina, ovaries and Fallopian tube

questions.explanation: The female reproductive tract is a system of organs that receive gametes (sperm), carry the egg, and house the developing embryo/fetus. This includes the vagina (receives sperm), cervix (passage), uterus (houses fetus), fallopian tubes (carry egg), and ovaries (produce egg). Option A lists the key parts.

questions.stem: A cell in mitotic prophase contains 20 chromosomes. How many chromatids does it contain altogether? a. 40 b. 20 c. 20 or 40, depending on when during prophase you look d. 10

options.C: 20 or 40, depending on when during prophase you look

questions.explanation: During prophase of mitosis, DNA has already been replicated in interphase. Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids. Therefore, if there are 20 chromosomes, there are 20 x 2 = 40 chromatids.

questions.stem: What process involves a series of cell migrations to form the three primary cell layers?
questions.explanation: Gastrulation involves a series of cell migrations to positions where they will form the three primary cell layers.

questions.stem: Which one of the following best typifies the expression 'universal currency of energy exchange'?
questions.explanation: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is often called the 'universal energy currency' of the cell because it captures chemical energy from the breakdown of molecules and releases it to fuel other cellular processes. It is used by all types of cells.

questions.stem: What is the action of the enzyme DNA ligase? a. DNA is broken up at a specific sites b. DNA fragments are joined together c. DNA replication occurs d. DNA transcription occurs

options.A: DNA is broken up at a specific sites

questions.explanation: DNA ligase is responsible for joining DNA fragments together by catalyzing the formation of phosphodiester bonds. It is crucial in DNA replication (joining Okazaki fragments) and DNA repair.

questions.stem: Cystic fibrosis is primarily caused by:

options.B: Changes or mutations in a gene(s)

questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is caused by changes or mutations in a gene(s), making it an example of a genetically caused congenital anomaly.

questions.stem: The paired up chromosomes at prophase 1 are often described as
questions.explanation: During prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair up to form structures called bivalents (or tetrads). Each bivalent consists of two homologous chromosomes (four chromatids total).

questions.stem: Examples of fission include single-celled organisms like amoeba, paramecium, and __________.
questions.explanation: Examples include single-celled organisms like amoeba, paramecium, and stentor.

questions.stem: What type of interaction is not typically involved in maintaining tertiary protein structure?
questions.explanation: Tertiary structure is stabilized by various interactions among R groups: hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, hydrophobic interactions, van der Waals forces, and disulfide bridges (covalent). Glycosidic linkages are bonds between sugars in carbohydrates, not involved in protein folding.

questions.stem: Alleles occupy identical loci on __________ chromosomes.
questions.explanation: Alleles occupy identical loci on homologous chromosomes.

questions.stem: How does temperature affect the efficiency of photosynthesis?

options.B: Affects enzyme activity; extreme temperatures inhibit photosynthetic enzymes

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis involves many enzyme-catalyzed reactions (like those in the Calvin cycle). Enzyme activity has an optimal temperature range; temperatures too low or too high will decrease efficiency.

questions.stem: ____ is the ability to maintain a constant internal environment in response to external environment changes
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment (e.g., temperature, pH, blood glucose) despite changes in the external environment. It is a key characteristic of living organisms.

questions.stem: DNA in eukaryotic cells is located mainly in the: A. Cytoplasm B. Ribosome C. Nucleus D. Membrane
questions.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, the vast majority of the cell's genetic material (DNA) is enclosed within the membrane-bound nucleus. Small amounts of DNA are also found in mitochondria and chloroplasts, but the main location is the nucleus.

questions.stem: In hermaphroditic species, what is the biological advantage of possessing both reproductive organs?

options.B: It increases the chances of successful mating in low-density populations
options.C: It eliminates the need for fertilization

questions.explanation: Hermaphroditism allows any individual to mate with any other, maximizing reproductive opportunities when mates are scarce.

questions.stem: Membrane phospholipids

options.A: Have hydrophilic heads that face outward & are exposed to water
options.B: Have hydrophobic tails that face inward & are shielded from water

questions.explanation: In the phospholipid bilayer, the hydrophilic (water-loving) heads face outward, interacting with the aqueous environments inside and outside the cell. The hydrophobic (water-fearing) tails face inward, away from water, forming the interior of the membrane.

questions.stem: Hypothesis is a necessity in scientific methods: a. Partially necessary b. False c. None of the above d. True
questions.explanation: The statement is true. The scientific method is based on forming and testing hypotheses. A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that guides an investigation. Without a hypothesis, an experiment lacks direction and a clear purpose.

questions.stem: It stores the cell's __________.
questions.explanation: The nucleus houses the cell's genome, encoded in DNA molecules organized into chromosomes.

questions.stem: Mendel's principle of segregation means that the germ cells always receive
questions.explanation: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that during gamete formation, the two alleles for a heritable trait separate (segregate) so that each gamete receives only one allele from each pair.

questions.stem: In a word, evolution means: a. nature b. change c. selection d. mutation
questions.explanation: At its simplest, evolution is 'change over time'. Specifically, it refers to the change in the heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations.

questions.stem: __________ is the process of crossing two genetically different individuals.
questions.explanation: Hybridization is the process of crossing two genetically different individuals.

questions.stem: Which extraembryonic membrane is primarily involved in waste storage and gas exchange in some vertebrates?
questions.explanation: The allantois stores metabolic waste (uric acid) in reptiles and birds. In mammals, its blood vessels become the umbilical vessels, and it contributes to the placenta's function in gas exchange.

questions.stem: Protein synthesis begins at the __________ codon (AUG).
questions.explanation: Protein synthesis begins at the start codon (AUG).

questions.stem: All biomolecules contain the element __________.
questions.explanation: All biomolecules contain the element carbon (C).

questions.stem: ________ discovered that capillaries link arteries to veins
questions.explanation: Marcello Malpighi, an Italian biologist and physician, was a pioneer of microscopy. He discovered the capillary network in the 1660s, providing the missing link in William Harvey's theory of blood circulation by showing how arteries and veins are connected.

questions.stem: The __________ phase is a resting phase for cells like nerve cells.
questions.explanation: G0 is a quiescent phase where cells exit the cell cycle and do not prepare for division (e.g., mature neurons).

questions.stem: As mitosis commences, a condensed chromosome consists of two: A. Centromeres B. Centrioles C. Kinetochores D. Chromatids
questions.explanation: By the beginning of mitosis (prophase), DNA has already been replicated during S phase. Each chromosome is now made up of two identical copies called sister chromatids, which are joined together at a common centromere.

questions.stem: Mitosis provides mechanism for quick reproduction in single celled organisms and for growth and reproduction in multicellular organisms.
questions.explanation: This statement is true. Mitosis serves different purposes depending on the organism. In unicellular organisms (like amoeba), mitosis is a form of asexual reproduction, creating two identical daughter cells. In multicellular organisms, mitosis is responsible for growth (increasing cell number), repair (replacing damaged cells), and in some cases, asexual reproduction (e.g., budding in hydra).

questions.stem: The correct order of taxa from largest to smallest is:
questions.explanation: The major taxonomic ranks, from broadest to most specific, are: Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. (A common mnemonic is 'Dear King Philip Came Over For Good Soup').

questions.stem: Epistasis refers to:

options.C: One gene masking the expression of another

questions.explanation: Epistasis is a phenomenon where the expression of one gene (the epistatic gene) masks or modifies the expression of another gene (the hypostatic gene). The phenotypic ratio deviates from typical Mendelian ratios.

questions.stem: Mitochondria play a key role in __________ (programmed cell death).
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release cytochrome c and other factors that trigger the caspase cascade, leading to controlled cell death (apoptosis).

questions.stem: _________ was the first to view living organism using a microscope
questions.explanation: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, a Dutch scientist, was the first to observe and describe living microorganisms (which he called 'animalcules'), such as bacteria and protozoa, using his high-quality, single-lens microscopes in the 1670s. Hooke had observed dead cell walls earlier.

questions.stem: Mendel’s principle of segregation implies that:

options.B: Each gamete receives one allele from each gene pair
options.C: Alleles can be blended in offspring

questions.explanation: The Law of Segregation states that the two alleles for a heritable character segregate (separate) during gamete formation and end up in different gametes. Therefore, a gamete carries only one allele for each inherited character.

questions.stem: What is the role of tradition in an associational society?

options.A: It promotes all aspects of life.

questions.explanation: In associational societies, 'the pervasive role of tradition is broken.'

questions.stem: Which of these is an approach to ecological studies? a. Competition approach b. Ecosystem approach c. Predation approach d. interaction approach
questions.explanation: The ecosystem approach is a major strategy for studying ecology. It involves studying the flow of energy and the cycling of materials between the biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components of a defined area.

questions.stem: Ova travel from the: ovary uterus fallopian tube.
questions.explanation: This sequence is incorrect. The correct pathway for an ovum (egg) is: Ovary -> Fallopian tube (oviduct) -> Uterus. The egg is released from the ovary into the fallopian tube, where fertilization may occur. It then travels to the uterus.

questions.stem: His famous Latin phrase was "__________" (all cells from cells).
questions.explanation: "Omnis cellula e cellula" is Virchow's famous phrase summarizing the principle of biogenesis for cells.

questions.stem: Which type of society is exemplified by the modern metropolis?
questions.explanation: Associational society, on the other hand, is exemplified by the modern metropolis.

questions.stem: During sexual intercourse approximately how many sperm cells enter the vagina?
questions.explanation: Approximately 300 million sperm cells enter the vagina during sexual intercourse.

questions.stem: A form of reproduction in which an embryo develops from an unfertilized egg is known as
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction in which an egg develops into an embryo without being fertilized by a sperm. It occurs naturally in some insects, fish, amphibians, and reptiles.

questions.stem: Mitochondria occupy about __________% of the cell volume.
questions.explanation: Liver cells are metabolically active, requiring significant ATP production, hence a high mitochondrial volume (~22%).

questions.stem: What is the most recent period, which continues today and includes all modern forms of life?
questions.explanation: The Quaternary Period (1.8 mya - present) is the most recent geological period. It continues today and includes all modern forms of life.

questions.stem: Which is not true about the subject biology?

options.A: It deals with all forms of life
options.B: It studies the origin & evolution of living matter
options.C: It may investigate the history of non-living matter
options.D: It analyzes cells and molecules in a cell

questions.explanation: Biology is the study of life and living organisms. While it encompasses the study of all forms of life (A), their origin and evolution (B), and their molecular and cellular composition (D), it does not investigate the history of non-living matter (C). That falls under the purview of geology, cosmology, or physics.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the mitochondrion in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell. They carry out the later stages of cellular respiration (the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation) to produce the majority of the cell's ATP.

questions.stem: The monomers of nucleic acids are called __________.
questions.explanation: The monomers of nucleic acids are called nucleotides.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a pollutant?
questions.explanation: A pollutant is a substance or energy introduced into the environment that has undesired effects, or adversely affects the usefulness of a resource. Water is not inherently a pollutant; it is a vital resource. However, water can become a pollutant if it is contaminated or in the wrong place (e.g., floodwater). In its natural state, it is not considered a pollutant.

questions.stem: The fusion of gametes creates a fertilized __________, which is diploid.
questions.explanation: Their fusion creates a fertilized zygote, which is diploid.

questions.stem: What term describes a level of organization that contains only one species? a. Community b. Ecosystem c. Population d. Biome
questions.explanation: A population is defined as a group of individuals of the same species living in a particular area at a given time. A community contains multiple species.

questions.stem: In ovarian cycle, the uterus prepares to receive fertilized eggs
questions.explanation: This statement is slightly misleading. The ovarian cycle refers to events in the ovary (follicle development, ovulation, corpus luteum formation). The menstrual (uterine) cycle refers to events in the uterus preparing to receive a fertilized egg. So, it's the uterine cycle where the uterus prepares, not the ovarian cycle.

questions.stem: DNA replication occurs during the __ phase of the cell cycle.
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs during the S phase of the cell cycle.

questions.stem: Kingdom Monera possess the following characteristics except: a. Unicellular b. Prokaryotic c. Eukaryotic d. Microscopic
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consisted of prokaryotic organisms. They lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Therefore, being 'eukaryotic' (having a true nucleus) is a characteristic they do NOT possess.

questions.stem: The corpus luteum forms from a ruptured follicle and produces LH.
questions.explanation: The first part is true: the corpus luteum forms from the remnants of a ruptured ovarian follicle after ovulation. However, it does not produce LH. It produces progesterone and estrogen. LH (Luteinizing Hormone) is produced by the anterior pituitary and is responsible for triggering ovulation and forming the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: Which of the following is testable in scientific enquiry?
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a testable statement in scientific inquiry.

questions.stem: The hollow structure from the invagination during gastrulation is called the: a. Progenitor b. Lanceletes c. Gut d. Archenteron
questions.explanation: The archenteron is the primitive gut that forms during gastrulation as a result of invagination. It is a cavity that will eventually develop into the digestive tract. The opening of the archenteron is the blastopore.

questions.stem: Sexual reproduction involves ______ division
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the formation of haploid gametes through meiosis. The fusion of gametes (fertilization) restores the diploid number. The resulting zygote then undergoes mitotic divisions to develop into an organism. So, meiosis is involved at some stages.

questions.stem: Translation is
questions.explanation: Translation is the process of protein synthesis where the genetic code carried by messenger RNA (mRNA) is 'translated' to assemble amino acids into a polypeptide chain on a ribosome. It is mRNA-directed.

questions.stem: The term community is used in ecology to describe all the: A. food webs in one ecosystem B. members of one species within a social organization C. species of plants and animals in a natural habitat D. species of plants and animals in one ecosystem

options.B: members of one species within a social organization
options.C: species of plants and animals in a natural habitat
options.D: species of plants and animals in one ecosystem

questions.explanation: An ecological community is the assemblage of all populations of different species (plants, animals, microbes) living and interacting within a particular ecosystem.

questions.stem: Normal cellular activities, such as protein synthesis, occur primarily during: A. Prophase B. Metaphase C. Anaphase D. Interphase
questions.explanation: Interphase is the period of the cell cycle when the cell is not dividing. It is during this time that the cell grows, carries out its normal metabolic functions (like protein synthesis), and replicates its DNA in preparation for division.

questions.stem: Study of fossils is: a. palaeontology b. palaeozoology c. Saurology d. Herpetology
questions.explanation: Paleontology is the scientific study of fossils, which are the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms. It encompasses various sub-disciplines like paleobotany (plants) and paleozoology (animals).

questions.stem: Intraspecific competition is competition among: A. species B. individuals of a population C. individuals of a community D. populations and their regulatory factors
questions.explanation: 'Intra' means within. Intraspecific competition is competition between individuals of the same species (within a population) for the same limited resources.

questions.stem: Which organelle contains hydrolytic enzymes and is involved in intracellular digestion?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs containing a variety of hydrolytic enzymes (acid hydrolases) that can break down all major classes of macromolecules. They digest materials taken in by endocytosis and recycle worn-out organelles.

questions.stem: The term ERGIC stands for: A. Endoplasmic Reticulum Golgi Intermediate Compartment B. Endoplasmic Reticulum Golgi Intermediate Complex C. Endoplasmic Reticulum Golgi Intermediate Configuration D. Endoplasmic Reticulum Golgi Intermediate Cytosol
questions.explanation: ERGIC stands for Endoplasmic Reticulum-Golgi Intermediate Compartment. It is a vesicular-tubular structure that acts as a sorting and transport station between the endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi apparatus.

questions.stem: The S phase is for __________ (lasting about 9 hours).
questions.explanation: The S (synthesis) phase is dedicated to DNA replication, where the entire genome is duplicated.

questions.stem: A symport protein transports:
questions.explanation: A symport protein transports two molecules in the same direction.

questions.stem: Double fertilization occurs in: a. Schizophyta b. Sporophyta c. Bryophyta d. Spermatophyta
questions.explanation: Double fertilization is a characteristic process unique to flowering plants (angiosperms), which belong to the division Spermatophyta (seed plants). It involves one sperm fusing with the egg to form the zygote, and another sperm fusing with two polar nuclei to form the triploid endosperm.

questions.stem: Cytokinesis is the division of the __________.
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm and organelles, completing cell division after nuclear division (mitosis).

questions.stem: In a hypotonic solution, an animal cell will:
questions.explanation: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration (higher water concentration) than the cell's cytoplasm. Water moves into the cell by osmosis, causing it to swell and potentially lyse (burst) because animal cells lack a rigid cell wall.

questions.stem: Which of these is not involved directly in translation? a. mRNA b. tRNA c. rRNA d. DNA
questions.explanation: Translation is the process of protein synthesis occurring at the ribosome. mRNA (carries the code), tRNA (brings amino acids), and rRNA (part of the ribosome structure and function) are all directly involved. DNA remains in the nucleus and is not directly involved in translation.

questions.stem: Diffusion does not require the cell to expend ATP. Therefore, diffusion is considered: a. Endocytosis b. Exocytosis c. Active transport d. Passive transport
questions.explanation: Any process that moves substances across a membrane without the direct expenditure of cellular energy (ATP) is classified as passive transport. Diffusion, facilitated diffusion, and osmosis are all examples of passive transport, driven by the kinetic energy of molecules.

questions.stem: What critical structure forms during gastrulation that determines the body axis of the embryo?
questions.explanation: In avian and mammalian embryos, the primitive streak is a groove that forms on the epiblast surface. It establishes the anterior-posterior axis and is the site where cells migrate inward during gastrulation to form the germ layers.

questions.stem: Which phase of the menstrual cycle is characterized by the thickening of the endometrial lining?
questions.explanation: During the follicular phase (which overlaps with the proliferative phase of the uterus), rising estrogen levels stimulate the repair and proliferation of the endometrial lining.

questions.stem: What constitutes the repeating unit of nucleic acids? a. phosphate molecules b. bases c. nucleotides d. sugar molecules
questions.explanation: The repeating unit (monomer) of a nucleic acid polymer is the nucleotide. A nucleotide is composed of a phosphate, a sugar, and a base.

questions.stem: Which feature of mitochondria is absent in prokaryotes?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) lack membrane-bound organelles. They have a single cell membrane and no internal compartmentalization like the double-membraned, highly compartmentalized mitochondria found in eukaryotes.

questions.stem: The Secretion of enzymes from the pancreas is a form of exocytosis.
questions.explanation: This statement is true. Exocytosis is the process by which cells expel materials in secretory vesicles. Pancreatic acinar cells produce digestive enzymes, which are packaged into vesicles. When the cell receives the appropriate signal, these vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane, releasing their enzyme contents into the pancreatic duct to be transported to the small intestine.

questions.stem: What is the base sequence of the DNA strand that would be complementary to the following single stranded DNA molecule 5' AGTTACCTGATCGTA 3'? a. 5' TCAATGGACTAGCAT 3' b. 3' TCAATGGACTAGCAT 5' c. 5' UCAAUGGACUAGCAU 3' d. 3' UCAAUGGACUAGCAU 5'
questions.explanation: DNA strands are antiparallel and complementary. For the given strand 5'-AGTTACCTGATCGTA-3', the complementary strand must be read in the opposite direction (3' to 5'). The base pairing rules are A-T and G-C. So, complement is 3'-TCAATGGACTAGCAT-5'. This matches option B.

questions.stem: The paired up chromosomes at prophase I are often described as: a. Bivalents b. Tetravalents c. Monovalents d. Trivalents
questions.explanation: During prophase I, homologous chromosomes pair up to form structures called bivalents (or tetrads). A bivalent consists of two chromosomes (a pair of homologues) and four chromatids total.

questions.stem: The study of the types or forms of interrelationships among a community of organisms within the same habitat is referred to as
questions.explanation: Synecology is the study of groups of organisms associated together as a unit (communities), focusing on the relationships between species within a community. Autecology is the study of individual species in relation to their environment.

questions.stem: Release of nitrogen from living animals to the soils occurs through: a. Excretion b. Decomposition c. Exhalation d. Putrefaction
questions.explanation: Animals release nitrogenous wastes (like urea, uric acid, ammonia) through excretion. These wastes are added to the soil and are then converted to ammonia by decomposers (ammonification).

questions.stem: Fungi differ from plants in that fungi:

options.C: Are heterotrophic and have chitin in their cell walls

questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic (they absorb nutrients from their environment) and their cell walls are made of chitin. Plants are autotrophic (photosynthetic) and have cell walls made of cellulose.

questions.stem: What is the term for the process by which the embryo undergoes differentiation and growth?
questions.explanation: Organogenesis is the process by which the embryo undergoes differentiation and growth.

questions.stem: Skin and associated glands form from which germ layer?
questions.explanation: The ectoderm is the outermost primary germ layer. It gives rise to the epidermis of the skin (including hair, nails, and skin glands like sweat and sebaceous glands), as well as the nervous system and the lining of the mouth and nostrils.

questions.stem: During which period did dinosaur populations peak and then go extinct, and flowering plants arise?
questions.explanation: During the Cretaceous Period (145-65 mya), dinosaur populations peaked and then went extinct (except for birds). Flowering plants (angiosperms) also arose during this time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct in the scientific naming of Rice
questions.explanation: According to binomial nomenclature rules, the genus name (Oryza) is capitalized, and the specific epithet (sativum) is lowercase. The entire name is italicized or underlined. So 'Oryza sativum' is correctly formatted.

questions.stem: Interactions ensure the smooth integration of all parts of a system so they function as a __________.
questions.explanation: Interactions ensure the smooth integration of all parts of a system so they function as a whole.

questions.stem: Each new strand is built using the old strand as a __________.
questions.explanation: Each new strand is built using the old strand as a template.

questions.stem: Which reproductive mechanism is often observed in fungi and some plants, allowing for reproduction without gametes?
questions.explanation: Spores are asexual reproductive units that are dispersed and can grow into new individuals without the need for fertilization. They are common in fungi, algae, and some plants like ferns.

questions.stem: Which stage of the cell cycle takes the longest duration to complete? A. G0 B. G1 C. S phase D. Mitosis
questions.explanation: The cell cycle consists of Interphase (G1, S, G2) and the Mitotic phase (M). Interphase is the longest phase, and within interphase, the G1 phase (first gap) is typically the longest, taking up a significant portion of the cell's life for growth and normal functions. G0 is a quiescent stage some cells enter, but for actively dividing cells, G1 is longest.

questions.stem: How many pairs of autosomes do we find in human cell?
questions.explanation: Humans have a total of 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). Of these, 44 are autosomes (22 pairs) and 2 are sex chromosomes (1 pair, XX or XY).

questions.stem: Select the ODD one:
questions.explanation: Quaternary is a period in the Cenozoic era, while the others are Mesozoic eras.

questions.stem: The two functional groups in carboxylic acids are __________ & ___________
questions.explanation: This question seems to be describing an amino acid, not a carboxylic acid. A carboxylic acid has the functional group -COOH (carboxyl group). An amino acid has both an amino group (-NH2) and a carboxyl group (-COOH). Given the options, only A lists -NH2 and -COOH, which are the functional groups of an amino acid.

questions.stem: Some hermaphrodites, like corals, can also __________-fertilize.
questions.explanation: Some hermaphrodites, like corals, can also self-fertilize.

questions.stem: The core theme of biology is __________.
questions.explanation: The core theme of biology is evolution.

questions.stem: Which is found only in animal cells
questions.explanation: Centrioles are paired organelles found in animal cells that are involved in organizing the spindle fibers during cell division. They are not found in most plant cells or fungi. Plasmids are found in bacteria and some fungi and plants, not animal cells.

questions.stem: __________ demonstrated that DNA was the transforming principle.
questions.explanation: Oswald Avery demonstrated that DNA was the transforming principle.

questions.stem: In handwritten text, how should a scientific name be formatted?

options.C: The two names are underlined separately

questions.explanation: When writing a scientific name by hand, the two names should be underlined separately to indicate they should be italicized in print.

questions.stem: Which is not a vestigial organ in man? a. segmental muscles of abdomen b. coccyx c. third molar d. nails
questions.explanation: Nails are functional structures that protect the fingertips and aid in manipulation. Segmental abdominal muscles (remnants of muscle blocks), the coccyx (tailbone), and third molars (wisdom teeth) are all considered vestigial structures in humans.

questions.stem: What is the developmental stage from the start of cleavage until the ninth week called?
questions.explanation: The embryo is the developmental stage from the start of cleavage until the ninth week.

questions.stem: The __________ contains enzymes for the TCA cycle and fat oxidation.
questions.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix is the site of the Krebs (TCA) cycle and beta-oxidation of fatty acids.

questions.stem: Charles Darwin is famous for his theory of:
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin, an English naturalist, is famous for his theory of evolution by natural selection, which he developed after his voyage on the HMS Beagle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct? a. Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with guanine; thymine forms three hydrogen bonds with cytosine b. Adenine forms three hydrogen bonds with thymine; guanine forms two hydrogen bonds with cytosine c. Adenine forms three covalent bonds with thymine... d. Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with thymine; guanine forms three hydrogen bonds with cytosine

options.A: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with guanine; thymine forms three hydrogen bonds with cytosine
options.B: Adenine forms three hydrogen bonds with thymine; guanine forms two hydrogen bonds with cytosine
options.C: Adenine forms three covalent bonds with thymine...
options.D: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with thymine; guanine forms three hydrogen bonds with cytosine

questions.explanation: In DNA base pairing, Adenine (A) specifically pairs with Thymine (T) via two hydrogen bonds. Guanine (G) specifically pairs with Cytosine (C) via three hydrogen bonds. This specific pairing is crucial for the double helix structure and replication.

questions.stem: The four stages of nitrogen cycle do not include: a. Nitrification b. Denitrification c. Ammonification d. Deammonification
questions.explanation: The four main processes in the nitrogen cycle are: nitrogen fixation, nitrification, assimilation, ammonification (or decomposition), and denitrification. 'Deammonification' is not a standard term in the nitrogen cycle.

questions.stem: A molecule with the formula C5H10O5 is likely a:
questions.explanation: The formula C5H10O5 matches the general formula for a pentose sugar (a monosaccharide with 5 carbons), such as ribose or deoxyribose. The ratio of H to O is 2:1, characteristic of carbohydrates.

questions.stem: How are mitochondrial proteins encoded?

options.A: Mostly by nuclear DNA, some by mtDNA

questions.explanation: The vast majority (>99%) of mitochondrial proteins are encoded by nuclear DNA, synthesized on cytoplasmic ribosomes, and imported into the mitochondria. A small but crucial set (13 in humans) are encoded by the mitochondrial genome and synthesized within the organelle.

questions.stem: Archaea are different from other bacteria because they:
questions.explanation: Archaea (formerly Archaebacteria) are a distinct domain of prokaryotes known for thriving in extreme environments, such as hot springs, salt lakes, and deep-sea vents. They also differ from bacteria in their cell wall composition and molecular machinery.

questions.stem: Molecules form __________, which are small structures within cells.
questions.explanation: Molecules form organelles, which are small structures within cells.

questions.stem: They play a key role in __________, breaking down old organelles.
questions.explanation: Autophagy ("self-eating") is the process where lysosomes degrade worn-out or damaged organelles to recycle their components.

questions.stem: The synthesis of RNA from DNA is called __________.
questions.explanation: The synthesis of RNA from DNA is called transcription.

questions.stem: It regulates __________ expression.
questions.explanation: The nucleus controls which genes are transcribed into mRNA, thereby regulating gene expression.

questions.stem: The polymer "carbohydrate" consists of monomers called: a. Glucose b. Maltose c. Amylose d. Lactose
questions.explanation: The general monomer for carbohydrates are monosaccharides (simple sugars), and glucose is the most common example. Maltose (a disaccharide), amylose (a starch), and lactose (a disaccharide) are all polymers or oligomers made of monosaccharide units.

questions.stem: What is the biological importance of human gametes being haploid?

options.B: To ensure restoration of diploid number upon fertilization

questions.explanation: Haploid gametes (n) carry one set of chromosomes. Fertilization, the fusion of two gametes, restores the diploid (2n) chromosome number in the zygote, maintaining species-specific chromosome numbers across generations.

questions.stem: In parthenogenesis, which of the following occurs?

options.B: Development of an embryo from an unfertilized egg

questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction where an egg develops into a complete individual without being fertilized by a sperm cell.

questions.stem: In nitrogen fixation, the reduction of nitrogen gas to ammonia occurs due to the activities of: a. Haber's process b. Thunderstorm c. Nitrogen fixing bacteria d. Decomposers
questions.explanation: Biological nitrogen fixation is carried out by specialized microorganisms called nitrogen-fixing bacteria (e.g., Rhizobium in root nodules, free-living Azotobacter). They possess the enzyme nitrogenase, which converts N2 to NH3.

questions.stem: __________ fats have double bonds and are liquid at room temperature.
questions.explanation: Unsaturated fats have double bonds and are liquid at room temperature.

questions.stem: In what type of animals is parthenogenesis commonly observed?
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis, the development of an unfertilized egg into a new individual, is common in many insect species (like aphids) and some reptiles (like certain lizards and snakes).

questions.stem: The occurrence of differences among the individuals of the same species is known as
questions.explanation: Variation refers to the differences in genetic traits or characteristics among individuals of the same species. It is the raw material for natural selection.

questions.stem: Alleles control the contrasting characters of the same __________.
questions.explanation: Alleles control the contrasting characters of the same trait.

questions.stem: Meiosis is a "__________-way" process.
questions.explanation: Unlike the cyclical cell cycle, meiosis is a one-way process that leads to gamete formation and doesn't repeat.

questions.stem: Which of the following mechanisms favour cross-pollination?
questions.explanation: Protogyny is a condition where the female reproductive parts (stigma) mature before the male parts (anthers) in a flower. This prevents self-pollination and promotes cross-pollination. Homogamy (both parts mature at same time) and monoecious (separate male/female flowers on same plant) can allow selfing. Cleistogamy (flowers that never open) forces self-pollination.

questions.stem: The interactions among non-living environment is called
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are the non-living components of an ecosystem, such as sunlight, temperature, water, and soil. Interactions among these components are called abiotic interactions.

questions.stem: In which scenario is internal fertilization more advantageous than external fertilization?

options.A: In terrestrial environments where gametes need protection
options.B: In marine settings with plenty of water

questions.explanation: On land, gametes are vulnerable to desiccation. Internal fertilization, where sperm are deposited directly into the female's reproductive tract, protects gametes from drying out and increases the chances of successful fertilization.

questions.stem: The outer lips at the opening to the vagina.
questions.explanation: The labia majora are the outer, larger, and fleshy lips of the vulva. They protect the other external genitalia and contain sweat and oil-secreting glands.

questions.stem: In biology, __________ determines function.
questions.explanation: In biology, structure determines function.

questions.stem: Which of the following traits is not determined by a single gene?
questions.explanation: Height is a polygenic trait, influenced by the additive effects of multiple genes, as well as environmental factors. Widow's peak, blood type, and cystic fibrosis are examples of traits largely determined by single genes.

questions.stem: Down's syndrome is Trisomy 18
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Down syndrome is trisomy 21 (an extra copy of chromosome 21). Trisomy 18 is Edwards syndrome.

questions.stem: Which of the following respiratory parts of an insect is not cuticularized?
questions.explanation: The tracheal system in insects is lined with cuticle, which is shed during molting. However, the smallest branches, the tracheoles, are not cuticularized. They are thin-walled and fluid-filled, allowing for direct gas exchange with the tissues. Spiracles and stigmata are openings with cuticular valves.

questions.stem: In the G1 phase a normal cell may: a. stop dividing b. duplicate chromosomes c. replicate mitochondria d. double check process and readiness
questions.explanation: During G1, the cell grows and carries out its normal functions, which includes replicating organelles like mitochondria to prepare for eventual division. Chromosomes are duplicated in S phase. Checking readiness (DNA damage check) occurs at the G1/S checkpoint, and a cell may enter G0 (stop dividing) from G1.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most suitable to estimate the population of Tilapia fish in a pond? a. Quadrat b. Transect c. Direct counting d. Capture-recapture
questions.explanation: For mobile animals like fish in a pond, the capture-recapture (or mark-recapture) method is most suitable. A sample is captured, marked, released, and then a second sample is captured. The proportion of marked individuals in the second sample allows for an estimate of the total population.

questions.stem: A gene is a hereditary determining factor and consists of a continuous segment of __________.
questions.explanation: A gene is a hereditary determining factor and consists of a continuous segment of DNA.

questions.stem: Where is thrombokinase, important in clotting, synthesized?
questions.explanation: Thrombokinase (also known as thromboplastin) is an enzyme complex. Like all proteins, it is synthesized on ribosomes. While its specific cellular source can vary (e.g., damaged endothelial cells, platelets, or tissues releasing it), the site of its synthesis is the ribosome.

questions.stem: Which structure forms as a result of gastrulation and is responsible for establishing body axes?
questions.explanation: The primitive streak is a groove that forms on the surface of the blastula/epiblast during gastrulation; it defines the anterior-posterior axis and is the site where cells migrate inward to form new layers.

questions.stem: Who is the founder of the binomial system of nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus developed the binomial system of nomenclature. He proposed scientific names for plants in his book 'Species Plantarum' in 1753.

questions.stem: A gene with at least two alleles is said to be __________.
questions.explanation: A gene with at least two alleles is said to be polymorphic.

questions.stem: Which domain in the three-domain system includes 'true' bacteria?
questions.explanation: In the three-domain system, Domain Bacteria contains the 'true' bacteria, which are prokaryotes.

questions.stem: The causes of some congenital anomalies are attributed to:

options.B: A complex interaction of genetic predisposition and environmental factors

questions.explanation: Some congenital anomalies are attributed to a complex interaction of genetic predisposition and environmental factors.

questions.stem: In eukaryotes, a gene occupies a specific position on a chromosome called a __________.
questions.explanation: In eukaryotes, a gene occupies a specific position on a chromosome called a locus (plural: loci).

questions.stem: Maintaining an internal environment with an organism is called: a. Response to Stimuli b. Metabolism c. Homoeostasis d. Adaptation
questions.explanation: This is the definition of homeostasis (also spelled homoeostasis): the maintenance of a constant internal environment.

questions.stem: Which process pumps protons into the intermembrane space of mitochondria?
questions.explanation: As electrons pass through the protein complexes (I, III, and IV) of the electron transport chain, they provide energy to actively pump protons (H+) from the matrix into the intermembrane space.

questions.stem: +/+ interaction that is not obligatory is
questions.explanation: A +/+ interaction means both species benefit. In mutualism, the relationship is obligatory for survival (e.g., lichens). In protocooperation, both species benefit, but the relationship is not essential for their survival (e.g., cattle egrets and cows).

questions.stem: __________ cells possess membrane-bound organelles.
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells possess membrane-bound organelles.

questions.stem: Who first observed the division of cells?
questions.explanation: While Schwann and Schleiden proposed that cells are the basic units, it was Rudolf Virchow who, in 1855, made the crucial observation that cells arise from pre-existing cells through cell division. He summarized this with the phrase 'Omnis cellula e cellula'.

questions.stem: When is the DNA content of a cell doubled?
questions.explanation: DNA replication (synthesis) occurs during the S phase of interphase. This is when the cell's DNA content is precisely doubled in preparation for cell division. In anaphase, metaphase, and prophase, the DNA is already replicated and is being sorted.

questions.stem: Which of the following events is not correct with the time span associated with it in a normal human fetus?

options.A: the sex of the child is evident in week 10
options.B: the limbs are distinct and bones begin to form in week 8

questions.explanation: All the statements are generally correct for human embryonic/fetal development. The heart begins beating around week 4. Limb buds appear and bones begin forming by week 8. External genitalia develop and sex becomes evident by week 10-12. Therefore, 'none of the above' is correct.

questions.stem: A situation in which the phenotypes produced by two alleles are clearly expressed is called:
questions.explanation: Codominance occurs when both alleles are fully expressed in the phenotype.

questions.stem: A child with blood group genotype IAIB is born of a woman with genotype IBIB. The father could not be a man of genotype: A. IAIA B. IBIB C. IAIB D. IAIO
questions.explanation: The child is IAIB. The mother is IBIB, so she contributes an IB allele. Therefore, the child must have received the IA allele from the father. A father with genotype IBIB can only contribute IB alleles, not IA. So he cannot be the father.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic of communal societies regarding their literacy and homogeneity?
questions.explanation: A communal society is usually a comparatively small, isolated, non-literate, and homogenous society with a strong sense of group identity.

questions.stem: Examples of first organisms in detritus food chains are usually
questions.explanation: A detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter (detritus). The first living organisms to utilize this matter are decomposers, such as fungi (e.g., mushrooms) and bacteria. Wood is the detritus itself, not an organism feeding on it.

questions.stem: Which membrane transport process requires the hydrolysis of ATP?
questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient (from low to high concentration). This energetically unfavorable process requires direct input of energy, usually from the hydrolysis of ATP.

questions.stem: The sugar-phosphate backbone is connected by __________ bonds.
questions.explanation: The sugar-phosphate backbone is connected by covalent bonds.

questions.stem: What would be the result if synapsis and crossing over failed during meiosis I?

options.A: There would be no change in chromosome number
options.B: Genetic variation among gametes would significantly decrease
options.C: Mitotic errors would be more likely
options.D: Cells would become diploid instead of haploid

questions.explanation: Synapsis and crossing over are key mechanisms for generating novel allele combinations. Their failure would drastically reduce genetic diversity in the resulting gametes.

questions.stem: Interkinesis is the stage between meiosis I & meiosis II
questions.explanation: True. Interkinesis is the period between meiosis I and meiosis II. It is usually short, and no DNA replication occurs. The chromosomes may partially decondense.

questions.stem: What is a community of organisms and their physical environment called?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem is a functional unit consisting of all the living organisms in a given area and their physical environment.

questions.stem: The group of organisms which interbreed freely is best described as a/ an _____
questions.explanation: A species is often defined as a group of organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring in nature. This is the biological species concept.

questions.stem: Which is a haploid cell?
questions.explanation: Haploid cells contain one complete set of chromosomes. In humans, the only haploid cells are the gametes: spermatozoa (sperm) in males and ova (eggs) in females. All other body cells (neurons, guard cells, cheek cells) are diploid.

questions.stem: Cells combine to make __________, a group of similar cells.
questions.explanation: Cells combine to make tissues, a group of similar cells.

questions.stem: What is the correct sequence of early embryonic development?
questions.explanation: Fertilization forms a zygote, which undergoes cleavage (cell division) to become a morula (solid ball). A fluid-filled cavity forms, creating a blastula. Gastrulation then forms the germ layers.

questions.stem: Which level of protein structure is characterized by α-helices and β-pleated sheets stabilized by hydrogen bonds?
questions.explanation: Secondary structure refers to local, repetitive folding patterns stabilized by hydrogen bonds between backbone atoms (not R groups). The most common patterns are the alpha helix and the beta pleated sheet.

questions.stem: A location of an organism or group of organisms is called
questions.explanation: A habitat is the specific natural environment or location where an organism or a population lives. It is often described as the organism's 'address'.

questions.stem: Approximately how many species of organisms have scientists identified and described?
questions.explanation: Scientists have identified and described about 1.7 million species. They are unsure how many more remain to be discovered.

questions.stem: __________ can convert ammonia to nitrite
questions.explanation: Nitrification is a two-step process. Nitrosomonas is a genus of bacteria that oxidizes ammonia (NH3) to nitrite (NO2-). Nitrobacter then oxidizes nitrite to nitrate (NO3-).

questions.stem: An example of first organism to be found in a detritus food chain is usually: a. Wood b. Mushroom c. Carpet grass d. Grasshopper
questions.explanation: A detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter. Fungi like mushrooms (or other decomposers) are often the first organisms to colonize and break down this dead material, forming the base of the detritus food chain.

questions.stem: How is a cultivar name correctly written?

options.C: In plain text, capitalized, and set off by single quotes

questions.explanation: A cultivar name is written in plain text (not italicized), capitalized, and set off by single quotes, e.g., *Viburnum opulus* ‘Roseum’.

questions.stem: Biologists consider an object to be alive if it displays __________ of the properties of life.
questions.explanation: Biologists consider an object to be alive if it displays ALL of the properties of life.

questions.stem: Which biomolecule serves as the genetic blueprint? A. Protein B. Lipid C. Nucleic acid D. Carbohydrate
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids, specifically deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), serve as the genetic blueprint. DNA stores the hereditary information that guides the development and functioning of all living organisms.

questions.stem: Which scientist's work on bacteria helped to discredit the theory of spontaneous generation?
questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur, a French scientist, studied bacteria extensively and his experiments showed that life does not arise spontaneously from non-living matter.

questions.stem: New individuals are generated without the fusion of __________ and sperm.
questions.explanation: New individuals are generated without the fusion of egg and sperm.

questions.stem: What is the release of an egg from the ovary?
questions.explanation: Ovulation is the process in which a mature egg (ovum) is released from the ovary into the fallopian tube, where it may be fertilized.

questions.stem: Recessive alleles are symbolized with __________ letters.
questions.explanation: Recessive alleles are symbolized with small or lowercase letters.

questions.stem: ________ is the capacity of cells to extract energy from sources in the environment and use it to grow, live and reproduce
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the totality of an organism's chemical reactions. It is an emergent property of life that arises from interactions between molecules. It consists of energy-releasing (catabolic) and energy-consuming (anabolic) pathways that allow organisms to extract and use energy from their environment.

questions.stem: ____ prepares the uterus for a fertilized egg to implant: a. Luteinizing Hormone b. Progesterone c. Estrogen d. Follicle-Stimulating Hormone
questions.explanation: Progesterone, secreted by the corpus luteum after ovulation, is the key hormone that prepares the endometrium for implantation. It converts the proliferative endometrium into a secretory one, making it receptive to a fertilized egg and maintaining it for early pregnancy.

questions.stem: In humans, red-green colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait. If a man and a woman produce a colour-blind son, which of the following must be true? a. The mother carries the allele for colour blindness b. The father is colour-blind c. Neither parent carries the allele for colour blindness d. The father carries the allele for colour blindness

options.A: The mother carries the allele for colour blindness
options.C: Neither parent carries the allele for colour blindness
options.D: The father carries the allele for colour blindness

questions.explanation: For an X-linked recessive trait, a son inherits his X chromosome from his mother and his Y chromosome from his father. Therefore, if a son is color-blind, he must have received the recessive allele on the X chromosome from his mother. The mother could be a carrier (heterozygous) or affected (homozygous recessive).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a characteristic of living things?
questions.explanation: All living organisms eventually die; immortality is not a characteristic of life. Key characteristics of life include order, reproduction, growth and development, energy processing, response to the environment, regulation, and evolutionary adaptation.

questions.stem: Thermometer is to temperature as secchi disc is to: a. pressure b. incubator c. sunlight d. water turbidity
questions.explanation: A Secchi disc is a simple device used to measure water clarity or turbidity by lowering it into the water and noting the depth at which it disappears from view. Thermometer measures temperature, Secchi disc measures turbidity.

questions.stem: _________ coined the term ecology
questions.explanation: The term 'ecology' (from Greek 'oikos', meaning 'house') was coined by the German biologist Ernst Haeckel in 1866.

questions.stem: Living things undergo __________ & __________ throughout life.
questions.explanation: Living things undergo growth & development throughout life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an output of the Citric Acid cycle?
questions.explanation: For each acetyl-CoA that enters the citric acid cycle, the outputs are 2 CO2, 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 ATP (or GTP). So, all the listed options are correct.

questions.stem: The process by which water moves from the atmospheres to the soil is called
questions.explanation: Precipitation is the process where water (in liquid or solid form) falls from the atmosphere to the Earth's surface. This includes rain, snow, sleet, and hail. Condensation is the formation of clouds.

questions.stem: is the capacity of cells to extract energy from sources in the environment and use it to grow, live and reproduce: A. Metabolism B. Reproduction C. Homeostasis D. Inheritance
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions in an organism. A key part of metabolism is extracting energy from the environment (e.g., from food or sunlight) and using it to power processes like growth, maintenance, and reproduction.

questions.stem: What is a key development during the third trimester?

options.A: Formation of the three germ layers

questions.explanation: During the third trimester, footprints and fingerprints are formed.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be considered as a direct evidence of evolution? a. Classification b. Comparative anatomy c. Fossils record d. Comparative embryology
questions.explanation: The fossil record provides direct evidence of evolution by showing the actual remains or traces of organisms that lived in the past. It documents the history of life and the succession of forms over time. The other options provide indirect evidence.

questions.stem: Nucleoside consists of: a. phosphates and bases b. bases and sugar c. phosphate and sugar d. phosphate, base and sugar
questions.explanation: A nucleoside is a molecule formed by a nitrogenous base bonded to a five-carbon sugar (ribose or deoxyribose). It does not include the phosphate group(s). A nucleotide includes the phosphate.

questions.stem: What is the role of helicase in DNA replication?

options.B: Adding nucleotides to the growing strand

questions.explanation: Helicase is an enzyme that uses ATP to break hydrogen bonds between base pairs, unwinding the DNA double helix ahead of the replication fork to create two single-stranded templates.

questions.stem: All cells possess a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, genetic material, and __________.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are universal cellular machines for protein synthesis, found in all cell types (prokaryotes and eukaryotes).

questions.stem: The interactions among non-living environment is called:
questions.explanation: The interactions among non-living environment are called abiotic interactions.

questions.stem: Vitamin K can be synthesized with the help of sunlight
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin with the help of sunlight. Vitamin K is synthesized by bacteria in the large intestine and is also obtained from dietary sources like green leafy vegetables.

questions.stem: The primary structure of a protein refers to: A. Alpha helix b. 3D folding c. Sequence of amino acids d. Association of subunits
questions.explanation: The primary structure of a protein is the linear sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain. This sequence is determined by the gene encoding the protein. The alpha helix is a secondary structure, 3D folding is tertiary, and subunit association is quaternary.

questions.stem: The __________ strand is synthesized continuously toward the replication fork.
questions.explanation: The leading strand is synthesized continuously toward the replication fork.

questions.stem: Which of these membranes act primarily as a 'bladder' for storing excretory products during the embryonic development in reptiles and birds?
questions.explanation: The allantois is an extra-embryonic membrane that stores metabolic waste products (uric acid) from the embryo in reptiles and birds. It also fuses with the chorion to form the chorioallantoic membrane for gas exchange.

questions.stem: Chloroplasts are __________ membrane-bound organelles.
questions.explanation: Like mitochondria, chloroplasts have a double membrane: an outer and inner envelope membrane.

questions.stem: In which system of nomenclature is a subspecific name, such as a variety name, added to the genus and species?
questions.explanation: Trinomial nomenclature, proposed by Huxley and Stricklandt, uses three names: the genus, species, and a subspecific name (like a variety).

questions.stem: _______ occurs about two weeks before a woman's period.
questions.explanation: In a typical 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation (the release of an egg) occurs around day 14. Menstruation marks day 1 of the next cycle. Therefore, ovulation occurs approximately two weeks before the next menstrual period.

questions.stem: Eukaryotes have ____ Ribosomes
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells have larger 80S ribosomes. Prokaryotic cells have smaller 70S ribosomes. The 'S' stands for Svedberg units, a measure of sedimentation rate during centrifugation.

questions.stem: What occurs during the acrosomal reaction that facilitates fertilization?

options.A: Enzymes released to penetrate the egg’s outer layer
options.B: Chromatin condenses in the sperm nucleus

questions.explanation: The acrosomal reaction involves the release of digestive enzymes from the sperm's acrosome, allowing it to break through the egg's protective barriers.

questions.stem: The number of individuals per unit area is described as: A. a population size B. a population group C. population density D. population frequency
questions.explanation: Population density is a measurement of population size per unit area or volume. It describes how crowded a population is. For example, the number of oak trees per square kilometer.

questions.stem: What is one of the major significances of culture regarding human survival?

options.B: It provides the knowledge and techniques that enable mankind to survive, both physically and socially.

questions.explanation: Another major significance of culture is that it provides the knowledge and techniques that enable mankind to survive, both physically and socially; and to master and control, as much as possible, the world around him.

questions.stem: Mendel conducted his experiments on the garden __________.
questions.explanation: Mendel conducted his experiments on the garden pea.

questions.stem: Meiosis II is similar to __________.
questions.explanation: Meiosis II resembles mitosis: sister chromatids separate in an equational division.

questions.stem: What does it mean to say that the characteristic of an organism is heritable? The characteristic: A. Evolves B. can be passed on to offspring C. advantageous to the offspring D. vary in population

options.B: can be passed on to offspring

questions.explanation: A heritable characteristic is one that can be transmitted from parents to offspring via genetic information. It is encoded in the genes and can be inherited.

questions.stem: In turner's syndrome, the individual is a sterile male
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Individuals with Turner syndrome (XO) are phenotypically female, not male. They are sterile due to underdeveloped ovaries.

questions.stem: The core theme of biology is: a. natural selection b. adaptation c. competition d. evolution
questions.explanation: Evolution is considered the core or overarching theme of biology because it explains the unity and diversity of life, the origin of adaptations, and the relationships among all organisms. Natural selection is a primary mechanism of evolution.

questions.stem: These are stacked to form __________ (singular: granum).
questions.explanation: A stack of thylakoids is called a granum (plural: grana).

questions.stem: What is the primary function of peroxisomes in eukaryotic cells?

options.C: Detoxification and breakdown of fatty acids

questions.explanation: Peroxisomes contain enzymes that break down very long chain fatty acids via beta-oxidation. They also detoxify harmful substances like alcohol and produce hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), which they then break down.

questions.stem: A chromosome with a diffused centromere that makes it have centromeric effect all along the chromosome is called: a. Holocentric b. Acrocentric c. Sub-metacentric d. Metacentric
questions.explanation: Holocentric chromosomes have a diffuse centromere, meaning the kinetochore activity is spread along the entire length of the chromosome. Spindle fibers attach along the whole chromosome. This is found in some organisms like nematodes and certain plants.

questions.stem: Turner's syndrome is XO
questions.explanation: True. Turner syndrome is a condition where a female is partially or completely missing one X chromosome, resulting in a karyotype of 45,X or 45,XO.

questions.stem: Which process increases beneficial mutations and eliminates harmful ones?
questions.explanation: Natural selection is the procedure by which good mutations are increased and bad mutations are wiped out over time.

questions.stem: The genetic code is __________, meaning multiple codons can code for the same amino acid.
questions.explanation: The genetic code is degenerate/redundant, meaning multiple codons can code for the same amino acid.

questions.stem: A correlation exists between the structure and function of a cell
questions.explanation: This is a fundamental principle of biology, often called the structure-function relationship. The way a cell (or any biological structure) is built directly relates to the job it performs. For example, the long, tail-like structure of a sperm cell allows it to swim, and the thin, flat shape of a red blood cell maximizes its surface area for gas exchange.

questions.stem: Why does sexual reproduction contribute more significantly to evolution than asexual reproduction?

options.B: It increases genetic variation via recombination and independent assortment

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction shuffles alleles through crossing over and independent assortment during meiosis and combines them randomly during fertilization. This generates novel genetic combinations, providing the raw material for natural selection.

questions.stem: Steroids are lipids synthesized from alkaloids
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Steroids are lipids, but they are synthesized from a specific lipid precursor called cholesterol (which is itself a steroid). Alkaloids are a different class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds found in plants.

questions.stem: The bonds between amino acids are __________ bonds.
questions.explanation: The bonds between amino acids are peptide bonds.

questions.stem: What is the general term for structural or functional differences present at birth that affect any part of the body?
questions.explanation: Congenital anomalies, also known as birth defects, are structural or functional differences present at birth affecting any part of the body.

questions.stem: The __________ is the genetic makeup of an organism.
questions.explanation: The genotype is the genetic makeup of an organism.

questions.stem: Mitosis results in two cells, while meiosis results in ____ haploid cells
