questions.explanation: Mitosis of a diploid cell produces two diploid daughter cells. Meiosis of a diploid cell involves two divisions and produces four haploid daughter cells (gametes).

questions.stem: Which molecule acts as a carbon dioxide acceptor in the Calvin cycle?
questions.explanation: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) is the five-carbon sugar that combines with CO2 in the first step of the Calvin cycle, catalyzed by RuBisCO.

questions.stem: Identify the odd one from the following: a. Mons pubis b. Fimbriae c. Clitoris d. Labia minora
questions.explanation: The mons pubis, clitoris, and labia minora are all parts of the external female genitalia (vulva). Fimbriae are finger-like projections at the end of the fallopian tubes that help guide the egg from the ovary into the tube; they are internal structures.

questions.stem: ___________ is the combination of the spatial habitat & functional relationship of an organism with its environment
questions.explanation: An ecological niche is the role and position a species has in its environment, encompassing its habitat (where it lives) and its functional relationships (how it gets food, interacts with other species, etc.). Habitat is just the physical location.

questions.stem: lamins are inside, next to nucleoplasm while ........... lamins are near the nuclear envelope.
questions.explanation: There are two main types of lamins. A-type lamins are found in the interior of the nucleus, next to the nucleoplasm. B-type lamins are associated with the inner nuclear membrane (near the nuclear envelope) and help anchor the nuclear lamina to the membrane.

questions.stem: Biological organisation does not move from one structural level to another
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Biological organization is hierarchical, meaning it moves from one structural level to the next, increasing in complexity. It begins with atoms, which form molecules, which organize into organelles, then cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, and finally the biosphere.

questions.stem: Clusters of rRNA where ribosomes are assembled are called
questions.explanation: The nucleolus (plural: nucleoli) is a dense region within the nucleus where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is transcribed from DNA and combined with proteins to assemble ribosomal subunits.

questions.stem: It is also the basis for __________ reproduction.
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction (e.g., budding, fragmentation) relies on mitosis to produce genetically identical offspring.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the relationship between light intensity and photosynthetic rate?

options.B: It increases rate up to a saturation point, then plateaus

questions.explanation: Initially, the photosynthetic rate increases linearly with light intensity as more photons are available to drive the light reactions. Eventually, another factor (like CO2 concentration or enzyme activity) becomes limiting, and the rate levels off.

questions.stem: Kranz anatomy is present in
questions.explanation: Kranz anatomy is a specialized structure in the leaves of C4 plants. It involves two distinct types of photosynthetic cells: mesophyll cells and bundle sheath cells, arranged in a wreath-like pattern around the veins. This anatomy facilitates the C4 carbon fixation pathway.

questions.stem: Which phase of respiration occurs outside mitochondria but feeds into mitochondrial pathways?
questions.explanation: Glycolysis is the breakdown of glucose into pyruvate. It occurs in the cytoplasm. The pyruvate is then transported into the mitochondrial matrix to be converted to acetyl-CoA for the Krebs cycle.

questions.stem: The binomial system assigns to each organism a unique name that describes its: a. family and species b. genus and species c. evolutionary history d. body plan and habitat
questions.explanation: The unique two-part scientific name in binomial nomenclature consists of the genus name and the specific epithet (species name). This combination is unique to each species.

questions.stem: Each stage is subdivided into __________ phases.
questions.explanation: Both Meiosis I and Meiosis II have four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.

questions.stem: The monomer in a single DNA strand in all living thing is
questions.explanation: The monomer, or building block, of DNA is a nucleotide. Each nucleotide consists of a phosphate, a sugar (deoxyribose), and a nitrogenous base. A nucleoside is just the sugar and base (no phosphate).

questions.stem: Membrane phospholipids: a. Have hydrophilic heads that face outward & are exposed to water b. Have hydrophobic tails that face inward & are shielded from water c. Both A & B are correct d. None is correct

options.A: Have hydrophilic heads that face outward & are exposed to water
options.B: Have hydrophobic tails that face inward & are shielded from water

questions.explanation: This arrangement is the fundamental property of the phospholipid bilayer. The hydrophilic heads are oriented outward, interacting with the aqueous extracellular and intracellular environments. The hydrophobic tails are oriented inward, away from water, creating a stable barrier.

questions.stem: The chart below is a simple representation of the nitrogen cycle. T humus N2 animals S V Plants NO3 U NH3. To which processes do the letters S, T, U and V refer?

options.A: denitrification, nitrogen fixation, nitrification, nitrogen fixation
options.B: nitrogen fixation, nitrogen fixation, denitrification, nitrification
options.C: nitrogen fixation, denitrification, nitrification, nitrogen fixation

questions.explanation: From the diagram: S is the process from atmospheric N2 going to plants/NO3? The diagram is a bit unclear, but standard cycles show: S: N2 -> Plants (likely through bacteria in soil/roots) is Nitrogen Fixation. T: Humus -> N2 (releasing N2 back to atmosphere) is Denitrification. U: NH3 (ammonia) -> NO3 (nitrate) is Nitrification. V: NO3 -> Plants (uptake) is not a specific process like the others, but in the context, it might be Nitrogen Fixation? Option C lists S: nitrogen fixation, T: denitrification, U: nitrification, V: nitrogen fixation. This is the most common set of processes in a simple N-cycle diagram.

questions.stem: What is the correct order of the Linnaean hierarchy from the most general to the most specific?

options.A: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
options.B: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
options.C: Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus
options.D: Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species

questions.explanation: The Linnaean hierarchy is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species, with Kingdom being the most general and Species being the most specific.

questions.stem: An example is __________ disease, caused by lipid accumulation in brain cells.
questions.explanation: Tay-Sachs disease results from a deficiency of hexosaminidase A, leading to GM2 ganglioside accumulation in neurons, causing severe neurological symptoms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is found in the nucleus? a. Ribosome b. Centrosome c. Vacuole d. Nucleolus
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a distinct, dense structure found inside the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. It is the site of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis and ribosome subunit assembly. Ribosomes are found in the cytoplasm or on the RER, centrosomes are near the nucleus, and vacuoles are in the cytoplasm.

questions.stem: Fossils are most commonly preserved in: a. molten magma b. metamorphic rocks c. igneous rock d. sedimentary rocks
questions.explanation: Fossils are almost exclusively found in sedimentary rocks (like sandstone, limestone, shale). These rocks form from layers of sediment that can gently bury and preserve remains. Igneous rocks (from magma) and metamorphic rocks (altered by heat/pressure) would destroy organic remains.

questions.stem: All are events of the Mesozoic era except one

options.A: It was the age of Dinosaurs
options.B: It was the age of birds

questions.explanation: The Mesozoic era is famously the 'Age of Dinosaurs'. Gymnosperms (like conifers) were the dominant plants. Modern birds (Neornithes) appeared towards the end of the Mesozoic (Cretaceous) or early Cenozoic. Saying it was the 'Age of Birds' is incorrect, as birds diversified and became dominant in the following Cenozoic era. The Cenozoic is often called the 'Age of Mammals' and also the 'Age of Birds'.

questions.stem: The carrion feeders are organisms that feed on: a. dead organisms b. plankton c. plants d. corpses
questions.explanation: Carrion feeders, also known as scavengers, are organisms that feed on dead animal biomass, specifically carcasses or corpses. Vultures are a classic example.

questions.stem: Which taxonomic rank is broader than genus?
questions.explanation: In the taxonomic hierarchy, Order is a broader category that contains one or more families, which in turn contain genera.

questions.stem: Homologous structures suggest:
questions.explanation: Homologous structures are anatomical features in different species that are similar because they were inherited from a common ancestor, even if they now serve different functions (e.g., the forelimbs of humans, cats, whales, and bats).

questions.stem: Which one is a vestigial organ in man? a. nails b. coccyx c. hand d. leg
questions.explanation: A vestigial organ is a structure that has lost most or all of its original function through evolution. The coccyx, or tailbone, in humans is a vestigial remnant of the tail found in many other mammals. Nails, hands, and legs are functional.

questions.stem: What type of environmental exposure can disrupt fetal development due to its ionizing properties?
questions.explanation: Exposure to ionizing radiation is an environmental factor that can disrupt fetal development.

questions.stem: __________ is the inability of an allele to manifest in a heterozygous condition.
questions.explanation: Recessiveness is the inability of an allele to manifest in a heterozygous condition.

questions.stem: The Law of __________ states that some alleles are dominant and others are recessive.
questions.explanation: The Law of Dominance states that some alleles are dominant and others are recessive.

questions.stem: If a mother is a carrier for haemophilia (an X-linked disorder) and the father has haemophilia, what is the probability that their children will have the disease?
questions.explanation: Mother is carrier (XHXh), father has haemophilia (XhY). Possible offspring: XHXh (carrier daughter), XhXh (haemophilic daughter), XHY (normal son), XhY (haemophilic son). So, 2 out of 4 possible offspring (50%) have the disease (haemophilic daughter and haemophilic son).

questions.stem: A dominant allele masks or suppresses the expression of a __________ allele.
questions.explanation: A dominant allele masks or suppresses the expression of a recessive allele.

questions.stem: The __________ strand is synthesized discontinuously away from the fork in Okazaki fragments.
questions.explanation: The lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously away from the fork in Okazaki fragments.

questions.stem: Each daughter cell receives chromosomes identical in __________ and number to the parent.
questions.explanation: The genetic composition (DNA sequence) and chromosome number are preserved.

questions.stem: During G1, __________ occurs, where only selected genes are used.
questions.explanation: Differentiation involves cells specializing by expressing specific subsets of genes, often determined during G1.

questions.stem: The specific epithet can provide hints about the plant. What does the name *Erythrina senegalensis* likely indicate?
questions.explanation: The specific epithet 'senegalensis' likely indicates the origin of the plant, in this case, Senegal.

questions.stem: During gastrulation the interaction between cell surface molecules enables the migrating cells to adhere to one another and move as a single mass. (True/False)
questions.explanation: This is true. Gastrulation involves dramatic cell movements (invagination, involution, etc.) to form the three germ layers. Cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) on cell surfaces allow cells to recognize, adhere to each other, and move collectively in a coordinated manner.

questions.stem: The statement 'Nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution' is attributed to:
questions.explanation: This famous quote is attributed to the biologist Theodosius Dobzhansky, emphasizing the central importance of evolution in biology.

questions.stem: Artificial classification groups organisms based on what?
questions.explanation: Artificial classification groups organisms for the purposes of convenience, such as grouping people according to morphological characters like height, habitat, or size.

questions.stem: Kingdom Monera possesses the following characteristics except
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera consisted of prokaryotic organisms (bacteria and archaea). They are unicellular and lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles. They are not eukaryotes.

questions.stem: It regulates transport via __________ pores.
questions.explanation: Nuclear pores are large protein complexes that span the nuclear envelope, controlling the passage of molecules (like mRNA and proteins) between nucleus and cytoplasm.

questions.stem: Living things must __________ their own kind.
questions.explanation: Living things must reproduce their own kind.

questions.stem: The particular location of an organism in an ecosystem / The specific position or function of an organism in a place describes its: A. an ecological niche B. an ecosystem C. a biome D. a trophic location
questions.explanation: An ecological niche describes the functional role and position of a species in its environment. It encompasses not just its physical location (habitat), but also its interactions with other species (like what it eats, what eats it) and its use of resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method by which organisms use to regulate homeostasis: a. sweating b. taking a cool shower c. shivering d. change the flow of blood
questions.explanation: Sweating, shivering, and changing blood flow are internal physiological responses that help regulate body temperature (homeostasis). Taking a cool shower is an external, behavioral action, not an internal regulatory mechanism.

questions.stem: If a DNA strand has nitrogenous base sequence ATTGCC, the mRNA will have
questions.explanation: During transcription, mRNA is synthesized complementary to the DNA template strand, with Uracil (U) replacing Thymine (T). So, DNA A -> U, T -> A, T -> A, G -> C, C -> G, C -> G. This gives UAACGG.

questions.stem: Turner syndrome is caused by:

options.C: A mutation in the CFTR gene

questions.explanation: Turner syndrome is caused by missing an X chromosome.

questions.stem: Wild type refers to: a. the most common phenotype thought to be found in the natural population b. any mutant genotype c. rare phenotype observed in the natural population d. the most extreme mutant phenotype observed in an experiment

options.A: the most common phenotype thought to be found in the natural population
options.C: rare phenotype observed in the natural population
options.D: the most extreme mutant phenotype observed in an experiment

questions.explanation: Wild type is the term used to describe the typical, most common phenotype or genotype as it occurs in nature, in a natural population. It is the standard against which mutants are compared.

questions.stem: How does conjugation in some unicellular organisms differ from typical sexual reproduction?

options.B: It involves direct DNA transfer without gamete formation
options.D: It only occurs in diploid organisms

questions.explanation: Conjugation (e.g., in bacteria and some protists) involves the temporary union of two cells and the one-way transfer of genetic material (often a plasmid) through a conjugation tube. It does not involve the formation of true gametes or result in immediate offspring.

questions.stem: Which hormone maintains the uterine lining during the early stages of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Progesterone, secreted by the corpus luteum and later the placenta, is essential for maintaining the secretory endometrium and suppressing uterine contractions to support early pregnancy.

questions.stem: Documented examples of vertebrate parthenogenesis include the Komodo dragon and __________ shark.
questions.explanation: Documented examples include the Komodo dragon and hammerhead shark.

questions.stem: When a man mistakenly tramples on a black ant and the ant dies; what form of interaction has taken place? a. mutualism b. Commensalism c. Predation d. Amensalism
questions.explanation: Amensalism is a relationship where one organism is harmed or inhibited, while the other is unaffected. The man is unaffected by stepping on the ant, but the ant is killed. This is a classic example of amensalism.

questions.stem: Variables kept constant during an experiment are: A. Independent variables B. Dependent variables C. Standardized variables D. Random variables
questions.explanation: Variables that are kept the same (constant) throughout an experiment to ensure a fair test are called standardized variables (or controlled variables). They are not being tested or measured.

questions.stem: What critical event occurs during interphase for proper chromosome segregation?

options.A: DNA is replicated to form sister chromatids
options.B: Chromosomes condense and attach to spindle fibers

questions.explanation: During the S phase of interphase, the entire genome is duplicated, resulting in each chromosome consisting of two identical sister chromatids. This ensures each daughter cell receives a complete set.

questions.stem: __________ cells have a well-defined nucleus.
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells (from Greek 'eu' = true, 'karyon' = kernel/nucleus) have a true, membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.stem: The cohesion of water molecules is primarily due to:
questions.explanation: Cohesion is the attraction between like molecules. Water molecules cohere to each other due to the continuous formation and breaking of hydrogen bonds between the slightly positive hydrogen of one molecule and the slightly negative oxygen of another.

questions.stem: Animals obtain their amino acids from: a. Other animals b. Plants c. A,B d. Synthesis on their own
questions.explanation: Animals obtain amino acids by eating other organisms (plants or other animals). While animals can synthesize some amino acids (non-essential), they must obtain essential amino acids from their diet. The question is general, so the broad source is diet (plants or other animals).

questions.stem: The trophic level of a green plant in a food chain is
questions.explanation: Green plants are producers (autotrophs) and form the base of the food chain. They occupy the first trophic level.

questions.stem: Most of the ATP made during cellular respiration is generated by
questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation is the process that produces the majority of ATP in cellular respiration. It involves the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis, using energy from NADH and FADH2 to power ATP synthase.

questions.stem: Egg cells are diploid.
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Egg cells (ova) are gametes and are haploid (n). They contain one complete set of chromosomes (23 in humans). When a haploid sperm fertilizes a haploid egg, the resulting zygote is diploid (2n).

questions.stem: In tracing the path of sperm, you would mention vasa deferentia before
questions.explanation: The correct path of sperm is: Testes (production) -> Epididymis (maturation/storage) -> Vas Deferens -> Urethra (ejaculation). Therefore, the vas deferens comes before the urethra.

questions.stem: During translation, the codon AUG codes for which amino acid?
questions.explanation: AUG is the start codon and codes for the amino acid methionine in eukaryotes and a modified formylmethionine in prokaryotes. It also codes for methionine at internal positions.

questions.stem: Differentiation in cells reduces efficiency
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Cellular differentiation is the process by which cells become specialized in structure and function. This specialization greatly increases the overall efficiency of a multicellular organism. Instead of every cell trying to do everything, different cell types (e.g., muscle cells, nerve cells, red blood cells) become experts at a specific task, allowing the organism as a whole to function much more effectively.

questions.stem: The main function of chitin in arthropods is to:
questions.explanation: Chitin is a tough, nitrogen-containing polysaccharide that forms the exoskeleton of arthropods (insects, crustaceans) and the cell walls of fungi. It provides structural support and protection.

questions.stem: Within the nucleus, the __________ is responsible for rRNA synthesis.
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a dense region within the nucleus where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is transcribed and ribosome subunits are assembled.

questions.stem: "Chloros" means __________ and "Plastos" means formed.
questions.explanation: Chloroplast = "chloros" (green) + "plastos" (formed/molded), referring to the green, chlorophyll-containing plastid.

questions.stem: A symport protein transports
questions.explanation: Symport is a type of cotransport where two different molecules or ions are transported across a membrane in the same direction. An antiporter transports them in opposite directions. A uniporter transports a single molecule.

questions.stem: The theory of evolution indicates that: a. Monkeys evolved from men b. Man evolved from monkeys c. Man and Apes had a common ancestor d. Man evolved from dinosaurs

options.C: Man and Apes had a common ancestor

questions.explanation: Evolutionary theory proposes that humans and modern apes (like chimpanzees, gorillas, orangutans) share a common ancestor that lived millions of years ago. It does not say humans evolved directly from any modern ape species.

questions.stem: Membrane proteins can act as __________ to detect external signals.
questions.explanation: Receptor proteins bind specific signaling molecules (hormones, neurotransmitters) initiating a cellular response.

questions.stem: DNA polymerase ___ has proofreading ability.
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase III has proofreading ability.

questions.stem: What is a consequence of the high rate of migration and cultural diffusion in the contemporary world?

options.C: Cultures are unable to be static.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Indeed, it is impossible for culture to be static in the contemporary world because of the high rate of migration and cultural diffusion.'

questions.stem: Which maternal infection is listed as a teratogen that can disrupt fetal development?
questions.explanation: Maternal infections such as rubella are listed as teratogens that can disrupt normal fetal development and cause congenital abnormalities.

questions.stem: Organs are composed of tissues, which are composed of cells. This is an example of which characteristic of life? a. Living things have levels of organization b. Living things are adapted to their environment c. Living things respond to stimuli d. Living things grow and develop

options.A: Living things have levels of organization
options.B: Living things are adapted to their environment

questions.explanation: The fact that living things are structured in a hierarchy, from cells to tissues to organs to organ systems, demonstrates the characteristic of having levels of biological organization.

questions.stem: Nuclear lamina consists intermediate filaments ......... thick made up of polymers of lamin ranging from ......... in size.
questions.explanation: The nuclear lamina is about 40-90 nm thick and consists of lamin polymers with a molecular weight of 60-75 kDa.

questions.stem: A cell must have 3 things
questions.explanation: All cells, whether prokaryotic or eukaryotic, share three essential features: a plasma membrane that encloses the cell, cytoplasm (the jelly-like substance inside), and genetic material (DNA) that carries hereditary information. A nucleus and nuclear membrane are not present in prokaryotes.

questions.stem: Fragmentation and Regeneration occurs in certain annelid worms, __________, and sponges.
questions.explanation: This occurs in certain annelid worms, corals/cnidarians/tunicates, and sponges.

questions.stem: The cell was first described by
questions.explanation: In 1665, Robert Hooke, an English scientist, used a crude microscope to examine a thin slice of cork. He observed small, box-like compartments which he called 'cells'. While he saw only the dead cell walls, he was the first to describe and name them.

questions.stem: Using a general principle to forecast specific results is __________ reasoning.
questions.explanation: Using a general principle to forecast specific results is deductive reasoning.

questions.stem: One of the functions of the DNA is to: a. secrete vacuoles b. make copies of itself c. join amino acids to each other d. carry genetic information out of the nucleus

options.C: join amino acids to each other
options.D: carry genetic information out of the nucleus

questions.explanation: One of the primary functions of DNA is replication – making copies of itself. This is essential for passing genetic information to daughter cells during cell division. Carrying information out of the nucleus is the job of mRNA. Joining amino acids is done by ribosomes.

questions.stem: The family, in the context of society's broadest definition, can be considered what?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'The family in this circumstance becomes a mini society,' based on the broad definition of society as any human relationship.

questions.stem: What distinguishes holoblastic from meroblastic cleavage?

options.A: Holoblastic cleavage divides the entire egg, meroblastic only part of it
options.B: Holoblastic occurs in birds, meroblastic in mammals

questions.explanation: Holoblastic cleavage (complete) divides the entire egg cytoplasm, typical of isolecithal eggs. Meroblastic cleavage (incomplete) is restricted to a small disc of cytoplasm due to large amounts of yolk.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a section of the uterus? a. Epididymis b. Fundus c. Body d. Cervix
questions.explanation: The epididymis is part of the male reproductive system, where sperm mature and are stored. The uterus has three main sections: the fundus (top), the body (main part), and the cervix (neck).

questions.stem: The structural carbohydrate in plant cell walls is __________.
questions.explanation: The structural carbohydrate in plant cell walls is cellulose.

questions.stem: The opening to the uterus.
questions.explanation: The cervix is the lower, narrow part of the uterus that opens into the vagina. It acts as a passageway between the uterus and the vagina.

questions.stem: Meiosis is divided into two stages: Meiosis I and Meiosis __________.
questions.explanation: Meiosis consists of two consecutive divisions: Meiosis I and Meiosis II.

questions.stem: A heterozygous individual for sickle cell anemia is typically:

options.B: A carrier with some resistance to malaria

questions.explanation: Individuals heterozygous for the sickle cell allele (HbA HbS) have sickle cell trait. They are generally healthy but have some sickled cells, which provides a survival advantage against malaria in regions where malaria is endemic.

questions.stem: A __________ group goes through all steps of an experiment but lacks the factor being tested.
questions.explanation: A control group goes through all steps of an experiment but lacks the factor being tested.

questions.stem: During foetal development, oogonium begins meiosis but stops at
questions.explanation: In human females, oogonia (diploid germ cells) begin meiosis during fetal development. They progress through prophase I but then arrest at the diplotene stage of prophase I. These arrested cells are called primary oocytes and remain paused in this stage until puberty.

questions.stem: Simple sugars with 3-7 carbons are __________.
questions.explanation: Simple sugars with 3-7 carbons are monosaccharides.

questions.stem: A human cell containing 22 autosomes and a Y chromosome is

options.A: a somatic cell of a male

questions.explanation: A normal human somatic cell (body cell) has 44 autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes (XX or XY). A zygote would also be diploid. A cell with 22 autosomes is haploid. A haploid cell with a Y chromosome is a male gamete: a sperm cell. An ovum would have an X chromosome.

questions.stem: Which eon is subdivided into the Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic eras?
questions.explanation: The Phanerozoic Eon is subdivided into three major divisions: the Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic Eras.

questions.stem: How does photorespiration negatively impact plant efficiency?

options.B: Consumes oxygen and releases CO2, reducing carbon fixation

questions.explanation: Photorespiration occurs when RuBisCO binds O2 instead of CO2. This process consumes ATP and oxygen, releases previously fixed CO2, and does not produce sugar, thereby reducing photosynthetic efficiency.

questions.stem: All the factors that affect the wellbeing of an organism in a place form: A. the ecosystem B. the environment C. the habitat D. the biome
questions.explanation: The environment is the sum total of all external conditions and factors (both biotic and abiotic) that affect an organism's life, development, and survival.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains the amphipathic nature of phospholipids?

options.A: They have both hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails
options.D: They are used only in plant membranes

questions.explanation: Phospholipids have a hydrophilic ('water-loving') phosphate head and two hydrophobic ('water-fearing') hydrocarbon tails. This amphipathic structure is fundamental to the formation of lipid bilayers in cell membranes.

questions.stem: Which is not found in prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus. Their genetic material is located in a region called the nucleoid. They do have ribosomes (though 70S), and many have a cell wall and a capsule.

questions.stem: DNA has more oxygen than RNA
questions.explanation: This statement is false. The sugar in RNA is ribose, which has an -OH group on the 2' carbon. The sugar in DNA is deoxyribose, which lacks this oxygen atom (it has just a hydrogen at the 2' position). Therefore, RNA actually has more oxygen atoms than DNA.

questions.stem: Which macromolecule's monomers consist of a sugar, phosphate group, and nitrogenous base?
questions.explanation: The monomer of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) is a nucleotide, which is composed of a pentose sugar (deoxyribose or ribose), one or more phosphate groups, and a nitrogenous base (A, T/U, G, C).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not correct? a. The ectoderm forms the outer layer b. The endoderm lines the digestive tract c. The mesoderm partly fills the space between the endoderm and ectoderm d. Each germ layer contributes to each of the structures in the adult animal

options.A: The ectoderm forms the outer layer
options.B: The endoderm lines the digestive tract
options.C: The mesoderm partly fills the space between the endoderm and ectoderm
options.D: Each germ layer contributes to each of the structures in the adult animal

questions.explanation: This statement is incorrect. While each germ layer gives rise to a specific set of tissues and organs, they do not each contribute to *every* structure. For example, the ectoderm forms the skin and nervous system, but not the lining of the gut (endoderm) or muscles (mesoderm). They have distinct fates.

questions.stem: Proteins are made of smaller molecules called __________.
questions.explanation: Proteins are made of smaller molecules called amino acids.

questions.stem: The 'after taxes' (net gain) number of ATP produced during glycolysis is
questions.explanation: In glycolysis, 4 ATP are produced, but 2 ATP are used in the energy investment phase. The net gain is therefore 2 ATP per glucose molecule.

questions.stem: Besides activating the egg another role of a sperm is to carry to egg: a. ribosomes b. DNA c. mitochondria d. RNA
questions.explanation: The primary role of the sperm is to deliver the male's genetic material (DNA) to the egg. The sperm's head contains the highly compacted nucleus with the paternal DNA. While the sperm's mitochondria (in the midpiece) do enter the egg, they are typically degraded, and mitochondrial DNA is usually inherited from the mother. Ribosomes and RNA are not major components delivered by the sperm.

questions.stem: Which type of RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome during protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA (tRNA) molecules have an anticodon sequence that base-pairs with a complementary codon on mRNA. Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid at its 3' end, delivering it to the growing polypeptide chain at the ribosome.

questions.stem: Choose the set of traits that would complete this Punnett square. R r on top, R r on side.
questions.explanation: A Punnett square for a cross between two heterozygotes (Rr x Rr) yields the following genotypic combinations: Top row, left box: R from first and R from second = RR. Top row, right box: R from first and r from second = Rr. Bottom row, left box: r from first and R from second = Rr. Bottom row, right box: r from first and r from second = rr. So the square is filled with RR, Rr, Rr, rr.

questions.stem: Which of these denote plants that have been selected especially for a particular characteristic and are propagated to continue that particular trait?
questions.explanation: 'cv.' stands for cultivar (cultivated variety). A cultivar is a plant variety that has been produced in cultivation by selective breeding for desired characteristics and is maintained by propagation. Option A includes 'L' for Linnaeus (author citation). Option B includes 'var.' for natural variety. Option D includes 'x' for hybrid.

questions.stem: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by: a. binary fission b. budding c. fragmentation d. spore formation
questions.explanation: Both yeast (a fungus) and Hydra (an animal) commonly reproduce asexually by budding. In this process, a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent organism, grows, and eventually detaches to become a new, independent individual.

questions.stem: In the following: grass----grasscutter----tiger----man; the amount of energy that moves from the grasscutter to tiger is:
questions.explanation: Assuming the grasscutter is a primary consumer and the tiger is a secondary consumer, the energy transfer efficiency between these trophic levels is typically around 10%. So, about 10% of the energy in the grasscutter (the prey) is transferred to the tiger (the predator).

questions.stem: A form of ecology that deals with the study of individuals is known as: a. individual ecology b. autecology c. autoecology d. synecology
questions.explanation: Autecology is the branch of ecology that focuses on the study of individual organisms or populations of a single species in relation to their environment.

questions.stem: Evolution can occur through natural selection of __________.
questions.explanation: Evolution can occur through natural selection of adaptations.

questions.stem: The first step in germination of many seeds is?
questions.explanation: Imbibition is the process of water absorption by the seed. This is the initial, physical step that triggers the subsequent metabolic events. The water uptake causes the seed to swell, breaks the seed coat, and activates enzymes.

questions.stem: The rough ER is so named because it has an abundance of ........... on it
questions.explanation: The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is called 'rough' because its cytoplasmic surface is studded with ribosomes, which are the sites of protein synthesis.

questions.stem: As we go from Kingdom to Species in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics: a. Decreases b. Remains the same c. Increases d. Either increases or decreases
questions.explanation: As we move down the taxonomic hierarchy from the broadest category (Kingdom) to the most specific (Species), the organisms become more closely related. Therefore, the number of characteristics they share increases.

questions.stem: What is the probability that a male child will inherit an X-linked recessive allele from his father?
questions.explanation: A father contributes his Y chromosome to a son, not his X chromosome. Therefore, a son cannot inherit any X-linked allele from his father. The chance is 0%.

questions.stem: The RNA type that carries information from DNA to the site of protein synthesis is called: a. tRNA b. mRNA c. rRNA
questions.explanation: Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries the genetic information transcribed from DNA in the nucleus to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm, where it directs protein synthesis.

questions.stem: The idea that organisms can arise from non-living matter, such as bacteria appearing from a conducive environment, is known as:
questions.explanation: The Theory of Spontaneous Generation is the belief that living things can come into existence from non-living matter, like bacteria appearing from a conducive environment.

questions.stem: In external fertilization, what factor is most critical for successful gamete union?
questions.explanation: Because gametes are released into the environment, precise timing between males and females is essential to ensure sperm and egg are present simultaneously.

questions.stem: In parasitism, the parasite always

options.D: attaches and feeds on the host

questions.explanation: Parasitism is a symbiotic relationship where one organism (the parasite) lives on or in another (the host), from which it derives nutrients, causing harm to the host. The defining feature is that it attaches to (or lives in) and feeds on the host.

questions.stem: Double-membrane organelles include the Nucleus, Mitochondrion, and __________.
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts, like mitochondria and nuclei, are surrounded by two phospholipid bilayers.

questions.stem: Why might a species switch from sexual to asexual reproduction in harsh conditions?

options.A: Asexual reproduction is more energy-efficient and faster
options.B: Sexual reproduction is required for temperature regulation
options.C: Asexual reproduction ensures higher genetic diversity

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction can be faster, requires less energy (no need to find a mate, produce complex gametes, etc.), and allows a single individual to colonize a new area or persist when conditions are stressful.

questions.stem: Normal human gametes have 46 chromosomes.
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Normal human gametes (sperm and eggs) are haploid and contain 23 chromosomes. When they fuse during fertilization, the resulting zygote has the diploid number of 46 chromosomes.

questions.stem: What event signifies the transition from prophase to prometaphase in mitosis?

options.B: Disintegration of the nuclear envelope and spindle attachment to kinetochores

questions.explanation: The breakdown of the nuclear envelope and the attachment of spindle microtubules to kinetochores mark the beginning of prometaphase.

questions.stem: In Kreb's cycle, the hydrogen of malate is accepted by
questions.explanation: In the Krebs cycle, the conversion of malate to oxaloacetate is catalyzed by malate dehydrogenase. In this reaction, NAD+ is the electron (hydrogen) acceptor, being reduced to NADH.

questions.stem: Division of the cytoplasm is called
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis is the process of cell division where the cytoplasm of a single eukaryotic cell divides into two daughter cells. It usually occurs after karyokinesis (nuclear division).

questions.stem: Ecosystems are described as open systems because: a. they have input and output b. they have open gates c. they lack boundaries d. none of the above
questions.explanation: Ecosystems are considered open systems because they exchange both energy and matter with their surroundings. They have inputs (like solar energy, nutrients) and outputs (like heat, water loss).

questions.stem: What is considered the basic unit of ecological study?
questions.explanation: The individual organism is the fundamental unit upon which ecological interactions are built.

questions.stem: Eukaryotes can be __________ or multicellular and have a nucleus.
questions.explanation: Eukaryotes encompass both single-celled organisms (like protists and yeast) and multicellular organisms.

questions.stem: What is the implication of culture being 'dynamic'?

options.A: It remains the same across all societies.
options.B: It changes continuously, shedding some features and acquiring new ones.
options.C: It is fixed at the time of its creation.
options.D: It is only influenced by internal factors.

questions.explanation: The text states: 'Finally, it is necessary to emphasise once again the dynamic nature of culture. It changes continuously, shedding some features and acquiring new ones.'

questions.stem: Why are decomposers important in a food chain?

options.A: Other organisms cannot eat them because they are microscopic
options.B: They breakdown dead organisms & recycle nutrients
options.C: They produce their own food from the sun
options.D: They stop the flow of energy from one organism to another

questions.explanation: Decomposers (like bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter and waste products, releasing inorganic nutrients back into the soil or water. These nutrients are then taken up by producers, making decomposition essential for nutrient cycling.

questions.stem: What is formed by a group of similar organisms capable of interbreeding?
questions.explanation: A species is a group of individuals that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

questions.stem: The following statements are related to external fertilization. Choose the correct statements: I. The male and female gametes are formed and released simultaneously II. Only a few gametes are released into the medium III. Water is the medium in a majority of organisms exhibiting external fertilization IV. It presents wastage. a. I and V b. II and IV c. III and IV d. I and III
questions.explanation: In external fertilization, gametes are typically released into water (III), which is the medium. Many gametes are released (not a few, II is false) to increase chances of fertilization, leading to significant wastage (IV is true). They may not be released simultaneously (I is not always true). So, III and IV are correct.

questions.stem: What has often been the basis for discrimination between and among cultures, according to the text?

options.B: Differences in the advancement of the technological component.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'It is important for you to note that the difference in the advancement of the technological component of the different cultures of the world has often been the basis for discrimination between and among cultures.'

questions.stem: Precipitation in water cycle does not include: a. humidity b. rainfall c. dewls fall d. snow fall
questions.explanation: Precipitation is water released from clouds in any form (liquid or solid), including rain, snow, sleet, and dew. Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air, not a form of precipitation.

questions.stem: During which trimester do the circulatory and respiratory systems mature in preparation for air breathing?
questions.explanation: During the third trimester, the circulatory and respiratory systems mature in preparation for air breathing.

questions.stem: It is also called __________ division.
questions.explanation: Meiosis is called reduction division because it reduces the chromosome number by half.

questions.stem: Which cells are specifically targeted by meiosis, and what is their role?

options.B: Germ cells – production of gametes for reproduction

questions.explanation: Meiosis occurs specifically in germ cells, which are specialized cells in the gonads (ovaries and testes). Their role is to undergo meiosis to produce haploid gametes (eggs and sperm).

questions.stem: Which of the following occurs as a result of fertilization?

options.C: the final phase of spermatogenesis begins
options.D: another round of menstrual cycle begins

questions.explanation: Fertilization is the fusion of two haploid gametes (sperm and egg) to form a diploid zygote. This restores the diploid chromosome number (2n) characteristic of the species.

questions.stem: Lipids have high oxygen content & this is why they store & release more energy during oxidation
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Lipids store more energy precisely because they have a low oxygen content and a high proportion of carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds. These bonds release more energy when oxidized compared to the bonds involving oxygen found in carbohydrates.

questions.stem: What are the two broad categories of causes for congenital anomalies?
questions.explanation: Congenital anomalies can be caused by genetic factors or environmental factors.

questions.stem: ________ is a state in which the internal environment is being maintained within a tolerable range
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a stable internal environment, even when the external environment changes. This includes regulating factors like temperature, pH, and water balance to keep them within a tolerable range for survival.

questions.stem: In addition to the hormones estrogen and progesterone, the ovary also produces FSH.
questions.explanation: This statement is false. The ovaries produce estrogen and progesterone. FSH (Follicle-Stimulating Hormone) is produced and secreted by the anterior pituitary gland, not the ovaries. FSH acts on the ovaries to stimulate follicle development.

questions.stem: DNA contains the sugar __________.
questions.explanation: DNA contains the sugar deoxyribose.

questions.stem: What is a key characteristic of an associational society regarding its social structure?

options.B: Individuals must fit into a complex social structure.
options.C: It lacks any discernible social structure.
options.D: Social structure is entirely fluid and undefined.

questions.explanation: In an associational society, 'Individuals must fit into a complex social structure in which they occupy many statuses and play many different and frequently unrelated roles.'

questions.stem: A form of ecological pyramid that is mainly an inverse pyramid is usually used to represent: A. Population in a grassland B. Population in a forest C. Aquatic ecosystem
questions.explanation: In some aquatic ecosystems, the pyramid of biomass can be inverted. For example, the biomass of producers (phytoplankton) at a given time may be less than the biomass of primary consumers (zooplankton) that feed on them, because the phytoplankton reproduce very quickly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a form of bacteria? A. Cocci B. Bacilli C. Spirilla D. Paramecium
questions.explanation: Cocci (spherical), Bacilli (rod-shaped), and Spirilla (spiral-shaped) are all classifications of bacteria based on their morphology. Paramecium, however, is a single-celled eukaryotic organism belonging to the protist kingdom, not a bacterium.

questions.stem: The name of the organelle responsible for packaging & transportation of newly synthesized proteins is
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus (or Golgi body) is the organelle responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins (and lipids) into vesicles for transport to their final destinations, either within or outside the cell.

questions.stem: What is the correct binomial name for human beings?
questions.explanation: The correct binomial nomenclature for humans is Homo sapiens, with the genus name capitalized and the species name in lowercase.

questions.stem: What is a food web?

options.B: A diagram showing all the energy inputs
options.C: A complex network of feeding relationships

questions.explanation: A food web is a complex, interconnected network of multiple food chains within an ecosystem, showing how energy and nutrients move.

questions.stem: Which organelle is responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins for secretion?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus receives transport vesicles containing proteins from the rough ER. It modifies (e.g., adds carbohydrate tags), sorts, and packages them into new vesicles destined for the plasma membrane, lysosomes, or secretion.

questions.stem: The flow of genetic information is from DNA to __________ to Protein.
questions.explanation: The flow of genetic information is from DNA to RNA to Protein.

questions.stem: What are edaphic factors in the environment concerned with? A. animals B. the climate C. the soil D. topography
questions.explanation: Edaphic factors refer to the physical, chemical, and biological characteristics of the soil that influence the organisms living in it. These include soil texture, pH, mineral content, and organic matter.

questions.stem: The arrangement of soil particles is known as: a. Soil drainage b. soil texture c. soil profile d. soil density
questions.explanation: Soil texture refers to the relative proportions of different sized mineral particles (sand, silt, and clay) in the soil, which is essentially the arrangement of these particles.

questions.stem: The first cells are the __________
questions.explanation: The first cells to appear on Earth were prokaryotic cells, specifically bacteria-like organisms. They are simpler and lack a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. Viruses are not considered cells.

questions.stem: Which early theory of evolution proposed that life forms existed millions of years ago and will continue to be the same throughout eternity?
questions.explanation: The Theory of Eternity posits that there is no beginning and no end to the universe, and life forms have existed and will continue to exist unchanged throughout eternity.

questions.stem: An animal has 36 chromosomes in each of its body cells. How many of these chromosomes came from its male parent?
questions.explanation: In a diploid organism, half the chromosomes come from each parent. 36 / 2 = 18.

questions.stem: Which of the statements sums up "emergence"? a. the whole is greater than the sum of the parts b. only life displays emergence c. the sum of the parts is greater than the whole d. only apparent when an organism is studied at the atomic level

options.A: the whole is greater than the sum of the parts
options.C: the sum of the parts is greater than the whole
options.D: only apparent when an organism is studied at the atomic level

questions.explanation: Emergence is the concept that complex systems and patterns arise from the interaction of simpler parts, resulting in novel properties not predictable from the individual parts. The classic summary is 'the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.'

questions.stem: In DNA hydrogen bonds are formed between
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds are the key forces that hold the two strands of the DNA double helix together. They form specifically between complementary nitrogenous bases: adenine (A) with thymine (T) via two hydrogen bonds, and guanine (G) with cytosine (C) via three hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: Cytoskeleton is composed of __________ made of actin & _________ made of tubulin
questions.explanation: The cytoskeleton is a network of fibers. Microfilaments (also called actin filaments) are the thinnest and are made of the protein actin. Microtubules are the thickest and are hollow tubes made of the protein tubulin. Intermediate filaments are another type made of various proteins.

questions.stem: The two distinct groups of cells are __________ and __________.
questions.explanation: The two distinct groups of cells are prokaryotic and eukaryotic.

questions.stem: How many genotypes are produced by the 4 human blood groups: A, B, AB and O? A. 4 B. 6 C. 10 D. 8
questions.explanation: With three alleles (I^A, I^B, i), the number of possible genotypes is given by n(n+1)/2, where n is the number of alleles. So, 3(4)/2 = 6. The six genotypes are: I^A I^A, I^A i, I^B I^B, I^B i, I^A I^B, and i i.

questions.stem: The primary role of chloroplasts in plant cells is to:

options.A: Convert light energy to chemical energy via photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the organelles where photosynthesis occurs. They capture light energy and use it to synthesize organic molecules (like sugars) from carbon dioxide and water.

questions.stem: Which coenzyme is reduced during the Krebs cycle and donates electrons to the ETC?
questions.explanation: NAD+ is reduced to NADH during the oxidation reactions of the Krebs cycle (and glycolysis). NADH then donates its high-energy electrons to the electron transport chain (ETC) at Complex I.

questions.stem: In __________, homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents or tetrads.
questions.explanation: Zygotene is characterized by synapsis, where homologous chromosomes align and pair precisely.

questions.stem: A __________ cross involves parents differing in TWO pairs of alleles.
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross involves parents differing in TWO pairs of alleles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a function of proteins in the plasma membrane?
questions.explanation: Membrane proteins perform many functions: transport (channels, carriers), enzymatic activity, signal transduction (receptors), cell-cell recognition, intercellular joining, and attachment to the cytoskeleton. ATP synthesis is carried out by specific enzymes like ATP synthase, which is found in mitochondrial and chloroplast membranes, not typically in the general plasma membrane of animal/plant cells.

questions.stem: Filling of the contractile vacuole in Amoeba is a form of active transport
questions.explanation: This statement is true. The contractile vacuole in freshwater protists like Amoeba is an organelle that collects excess water that enters the cell by osmosis. Collecting this water into the vacuole requires the cell to actively transport ions into the vacuole, which creates an osmotic gradient that draws water in. This process of filling the vacuole, therefore, relies on active transport. The expulsion of the vacuole's contents is then a form of exocytosis.

questions.stem: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by
questions.explanation: Yeast (a fungus) and Hydra (a cnidarian) both commonly reproduce asexually by budding. A small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent, grows, and eventually detaches to become a new, independent individual.

questions.stem: Gametes are formed during the process of __________.
questions.explanation: Gametes are formed during the process of meiosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true of mitochondria of a cell? A. It is the powerhouse of the cells B. It is found in all cells C. They are sausage shaped cell D. They consist of two straight membranes separated by fluid-filled space

options.A: It is the powerhouse of the cells
options.B: It is found in all cells
options.D: They consist of two straight membranes separated by fluid-filled space

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are not found in all cells. They are absent in prokaryotic cells (which lack membrane-bound organelles altogether). They are also absent in a few eukaryotic cell types, such as mature mammalian red blood cells (erythrocytes). The other options are generally accurate descriptions.

questions.stem: Implantation is completed by the
questions.explanation: Implantation of the blastocyst into the endometrium begins around day 6-7 after fertilization and is usually completed by about day 11 or 12.

questions.stem: How many types of antigens are in ABO blood group? a. 1 b. 3 c. 2 d. 4
questions.explanation: The ABO blood group system involves two main types of antigens (A and B) on the surface of red blood cells. Type A has A antigens, type B has B antigens, type AB has both, and type O has neither.

questions.stem: What is the longest part of Earth's history trace fossils appeared? a. Paleozoic Era b. Precambrian Era c. Mesozoic Era d. Cenozoic Era
questions.explanation: The Precambrian is the longest part of Earth's history. While trace fossils (like microbial mats and burrows) do appear in the late Precambrian, abundant and diverse fossil life, including most trace fossils, appears in the subsequent Paleozoic Era.

questions.stem: This organelle is absent in plant cell: A. Xylem B. Mitochondrion C. Centriole D. Ribosome
questions.explanation: Centrioles are absent in most plant cells. Plant cells use other structures to organize their spindle fibers during cell division. Xylem is a complex tissue, not an organelle. Mitochondria and ribosomes are present in both plant and animal cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the correct order of development in human? a. Embryo- Zygote- Gamete- Foetus b. Zygote- Embryo- Gamete- Foetus c. Gamete- Zygote- Embryo- Foetus d. Gamete- Embryo- Zygote- Foetus
questions.explanation: The correct developmental order begins with gametes (sperm and egg). Their fusion forms a zygote. The zygote undergoes cleavage to become an embryo. After the embryonic period (up to 8 weeks), the developing human is called a fetus until birth. So, Gamete -> Zygote -> Embryo -> Foetus.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of asexual reproduction is correctly matched with its definition?

options.A: Binary fission – Parent splits into two identical individuals
options.C: Fragmentation – Two parents form a zygote
options.D: Sporulation – New organisms arise from flowers

questions.explanation: Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction where a single-celled organism divides its DNA and cytoplasm to form two genetically identical daughter cells of roughly equal size.

questions.stem: Which of the following structure is not involved in mitosis? A. Cell wall B. Chromosome C. Chromatid D. Centriole
questions.explanation: The cell wall is a structure found in plant cells, but it is not directly involved in the mechanics of mitosis. Chromosomes, chromatids, and centrioles (in animal cells) are all directly involved in the process of chromosome movement and division. Mitosis occurs inside the cell, with the cell wall acting as a boundary.

questions.stem: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) was developed in what year?
questions.explanation: The Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) was invented by Kary Mullis in 1983 while working at Cetus Corporation. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this invention in 1993.

questions.stem: They contain chlorophyll and accessory pigments called __________.
questions.explanation: Carotenoids (e.g., beta-carotene) are accessory pigments in chloroplasts that absorb different wavelengths of light and protect against photo-oxidation.

questions.stem: Energy and nutrients enter a community by way of the: A. producers B. consumers C. scavengers D. detritivores
questions.explanation: Producers are the entry point for both energy (from the sun) and nutrients (from the soil/water) into the biological community. They convert inorganic materials into organic forms that other organisms can use.

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents polygenic inheritance?
questions.explanation: Polygenic inheritance occurs when a single phenotypic trait is influenced by two or more genes. Human skin color is a classic example, influenced by multiple genes, resulting in a continuous range of phenotypes.

questions.stem: What is the main cell wall component of fungi?
questions.explanation: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, which is different from the cellulose found in plant cell walls.

questions.stem: __________ store oils and fats.
questions.explanation: Elaioplasts are leucoplasts that store lipids (oils and fats).

questions.stem: A human cell containing 22 autosomes and a Y chromosome is: A. a somatic cell of a male B. a zygote C. a sperm cell D. an ovum.

options.A: a somatic cell of a male

questions.explanation: A cell with 22 autosomes and a Y chromosome is haploid. A somatic cell in a male would have 44 autosomes + XY (total 46). A zygote would have 44 autosomes + XX or XY. An ovum has 22 autosomes + X. A sperm can have 22 autosomes + X or 22 autosomes + Y.

questions.stem: The bond that joins amino acids together to form protein is: a. Protein bond b. Peptone bond c. Amino bond d. Peptide bond e. B, C, D
questions.explanation: The specific covalent bond formed between two amino acids during protein synthesis is called a peptide bond. It is formed by a dehydration reaction between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next.

questions.stem: This envelope is continuous with the __________.
questions.explanation: The outer membrane of the nuclear envelope is studded with ribosomes and is continuous with the rough ER.

questions.stem: In plant cells, what is the function of the cell plate during cytokinesis?

options.A: Prevents the formation of the mitotic spindle
options.C: Facilitates the formation of a new cell wall between daughter cells

questions.explanation: In plant cells, vesicles from the Golgi apparatus coalesce at the metaphase plate to form a cell plate. This structure matures into a new cell wall that partitions the daughter cells.

questions.stem: What type of anatomical structures share a common structure but have different functions, providing evidence for common ancestry?
questions.explanation: Homologous structures share a common underlying structure but may have different functions, indicating they evolved from a common ancestor.

questions.stem: The plasma membrane is generally a double layer of __ & __: a. glycogen, proteins b. phospholipids, proteins c. glycoproteins, phospholipids d. lipids, glycoproteins
questions.explanation: The basic structural framework of the plasma membrane is the phospholipid bilayer. Proteins are embedded within or associated with this bilayer, performing various functions like transport and signaling. Glycoproteins and glycolipids are also present but are modified components.

questions.stem: In the hierarchy of the geologic history of life, the largest is the: a. Period b. Eon c.
questions.explanation: In the geologic time scale, Eons are the largest and most inclusive units of time, spanning billions of years. The Phanerozoic Eon, for example, covers the last ~541 million years.

questions.stem: Which category of plants is a 'cultivated variety' often propagated asexually to maintain a specific trait?
questions.explanation: A cultivar, which stands for 'cultivated variety', is a plant selected for a particular characteristic and is usually propagated asexually to maintain that trait.

questions.stem: How many types of alleles control traits in ABO blood group? a. 1 b. 3 c. 2 d. 4
questions.explanation: The ABO blood group system is controlled by a single gene with three common alleles: I^A, I^B, and i. I^A and I^B are codominant, and both are dominant over i.

questions.stem: During the G1 phase, __________ synthesis and growth occur.
questions.explanation: In G1 phase, the cell grows and synthesizes proteins needed for DNA replication and cell functions.

questions.stem: is a male part of the flower. a. Stamen b. Style c. Stigma d. Sepal
questions.explanation: The stamen is the male reproductive organ of a flower. It consists of the anther (where pollen is produced) and the filament (the stalk that supports the anther).

questions.stem: The two Greek words used to derive the word Ecology are Oikos and Logos. What does oikos mean? a. environment b. home c. land d. house
questions.explanation: The word Ecology is derived from the Greek words 'Oikos' meaning 'home' or 'place to live' and 'Logos' meaning 'study of'. So, ecology is literally the study of organisms in their home or environment.

questions.stem: Budding in yeast results in which of the following outcomes?

options.A: A smaller daughter cell detaches from the parent

questions.explanation: In budding, a small outgrowth or 'bud' forms on the parent cell. The nucleus divides, and one nucleus migrates into the bud, which grows and eventually pinches off as a smaller, genetically identical daughter cell.

questions.stem: The ability to taste PTC is a trait: A. dominant B. recessive C. sex controlled D. sex linked.
questions.explanation: The ability to taste the chemical PTC (phenylthiocarbamide) is an autosomal dominant trait. Individuals with at least one copy of the dominant allele (T) can taste it, while those homozygous recessive (tt) are non-tasters.

questions.stem: A nucleoside comprises of

options.A: a base, a sugar and phosphate

questions.explanation: A nucleoside is composed of a nitrogenous base bonded to a five-carbon sugar (ribose or deoxyribose). A nucleotide is a nucleoside with one or more phosphate groups attached.

questions.stem: DNA differs from RNA in that DNA:
questions.explanation: DNA contains the sugar deoxyribose and the nitrogenous bases adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G). RNA contains ribose and uses uracil (U) instead of thymine.

questions.stem: Where does implantation take place?
questions.explanation: Implantation takes place in the uterus.

questions.stem: Biologists study life from single cells to the global interactions of millions of __________.
questions.explanation: Biologists study life from single cells to the global interactions of millions of organisms.

questions.stem: A chromosome with two centromeres is called: a. Sub-metacentric b. Acentric c. Acrocentric d. Dicentric
questions.explanation: A dicentric chromosome is an abnormal chromosome with two centromeres. This can result from certain types of chromosomal rearrangements, like dicentric fusion. It can lead to problems during cell division as it may be pulled in two directions.

questions.stem: Individual's metaphase chromosomes organized by length, shape, centromere location is called
questions.explanation: A karyotype is the number and appearance of chromosomes in the nucleus. The term also refers to the process of pairing and ordering all the chromosomes of an organism based on their length, shape, and centromere position.

questions.stem: Stored energy reserves are provided by __________.
questions.explanation: Stored energy reserves are provided by lipids.

questions.stem: In a certain plant, the allele for white fruit W is dominant over the allele for yellow fruit w. A white-fruited plant was crossed with a yellow-fruited plant. About half of the offspring were white-fruited and the other half were yellow-fruited, which genotypes did the parent plants have? A. ww and ww B. Ww and ww C. WW and ww D. WW and Ww
questions.explanation: A 1:1 phenotypic ratio in offspring indicates a test cross: a heterozygous dominant crossed with a homozygous recessive. The white-fruited parent must be heterozygous (Ww) and the yellow-fruited parent is homozygous recessive (ww).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an evidence of evolution? a. Fossils b. Paleontology c. Artificial selection d. Embryology
questions.explanation: Paleontology is the *study* of fossils, which is a field of science that provides evidence for evolution. It is not itself a piece of evidence, but the discipline that uncovers and interprets the evidence (fossils). Fossils, artificial selection (as a demonstration of selection), and embryology are all lines of evidence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of chordates?
questions.explanation: The presence of a notochord is a defining characteristic of chordates.

questions.stem: Some species can reproduce without any form of __________.
questions.explanation: Some species can reproduce without any form of sex.

questions.stem: A __________ condition occurs when a gene is present in only one copy.
questions.explanation: A hemizygous condition occurs when a gene is present in only one copy.

questions.stem: Which of the following occurs as a result of fertilization? a. a gamete is formed b. diploidy is restored c. the final phase of spermatogenesis begins d. another round of menstrual cycle begins

options.C: the final phase of spermatogenesis begins
options.D: another round of menstrual cycle begins

questions.explanation: Fertilization is the fusion of two haploid gametes (sperm and egg) to form a diploid zygote. The zygote thus has a complete set of chromosomes (diploid number), restoring the diploid state characteristic of the species.

questions.stem: The number of nucleotides in a complete turn of the DNA double helix is
questions.explanation: In the classic B-form DNA double helix, one complete turn of the helix spans about 34 Å (angstroms) and contains 10 base pairs. Since each base pair consists of two nucleotides (one on each strand), a complete turn contains 10 base pairs * 2 nucleotides/base pair = 20 nucleotides. However, the question asks for nucleotides, not base pairs. Wait, the options include 10. Standard textbooks often state there are 10 base pairs per turn. The question says 'number of nucleotides'. 10 base pairs = 20 nucleotides. Option C is 10. This could be a common point of confusion. Given the options, 10 likely refers to base pairs. I'll answer based on the most common fact: 10 base pairs per turn, but the question asks for nucleotides. Let's check the provided options again. The options in the text are "A. 20 B. 15 C. 10 D. 25". 20 nucleotides is correct. However, many students might remember '10 base pairs' and pick C. The most accurate answer is A. 20. But given the question's wording and standard exam question patterns, they often ask 'base pairs' and answer 10. Since it explicitly says 'nucleotides', I must go with 20. My analysis says A is correct. The provided correct answer in the original text is C, which suggests they might have meant 'base pairs'. Following the question as written, I will select A.20. But to be safe, I'll include an explanation clarifying the base pair vs. nucleotide count.

questions.stem: The smallest and most fundamental unit of matter is the __________.
questions.explanation: The smallest and most fundamental unit of matter is the atom.

questions.stem: Unifying themes connect concepts from many fields of __________.
questions.explanation: Unifying themes connect concepts from many fields of biology.

questions.stem: Which of the following macromolecules does not undergo dehydration synthesis during polymer formation?
questions.explanation: Dehydration synthesis (condensation) is the process of linking monomers by removing a water molecule. Proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides are all formed this way. Simple lipids like triglycerides are also formed by dehydration (ester linkage), but other lipids like steroids are not polymers and are not assembled from monomers via dehydration synthesis.

questions.stem: What is the function of cytochrome c in mitochondria?

options.B: Transfers electrons between complexes III and IV

questions.explanation: Cytochrome c is a small, soluble protein located in the intermembrane space. It shuttles electrons from Complex III (cytochrome bc1 complex) to Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase).

questions.stem: What does the term "structure fits function" imply in Biology?

options.A: Structure of a part determines its function
options.B: All organisms have the same structure

questions.explanation: "Structure fits function" means the structure of a part determines its function.

questions.stem: A polysaccharide contains _____ units of monosaccharides chain
questions.explanation: A polysaccharide is a polymer made up of a large number (typically more than 10) of monosaccharide units joined by glycosidic bonds. Oligosaccharides consist of 2-10 units.

questions.stem: The F in F1 stands for __________, meaning son or offspring.
questions.explanation: The F in F1 stands for Filial, meaning son or offspring.

questions.stem: The process of releasing a mature ovum into the fallopian tubes each month.
questions.explanation: Ovulation is the phase in the menstrual cycle where a mature ovarian follicle ruptures and releases an egg (ovum) from the ovary. It typically occurs around day 14 of a 28-day cycle and releases the egg into the fallopian tube, where it may meet sperm.

questions.stem: Which one is milk ejection hormone? a. prolactin b. estrogen c. oxytocin d. relaxin
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is the hormone responsible for milk ejection (the 'let-down' reflex). It causes the contraction of myoepithelial cells around the milk-producing alveoli in the mammary glands, forcing milk into the ducts. Prolactin stimulates milk production.

questions.stem: In the Biblical injunction of creation, Creation of bird and fish was on: a. day 3 b. day 5 c. day 6 d. day 4
questions.explanation: According to the Biblical account in Genesis, on the fifth day, God created the creatures of the sea (fish) and the birds of the air.

questions.stem: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygotes (AaBb x AaBb), what is the expected phenotypic ratio?
questions.explanation: For two genes that assort independently, a cross between two dihybrid heterozygotes (AaBb) yields a classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio in the offspring: 9 with both dominant traits, 3 with one dominant/one recessive, 3 with the other dominant/other recessive, and 1 with both recessive traits.

questions.stem: Oestrogen& progesterone are some hormones essential for milk production in the breast
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Oestrogen and progesterone are essential for the development of the mammary glands (ducts and lobules) during puberty and pregnancy. However, the primary hormone that stimulates milk production (lactogenesis) after childbirth is prolactin. Oestrogen and progesterone actually inhibit milk production during pregnancy.

questions.stem: Living things maintain __________, an internal balance.
questions.explanation: Living things maintain homeostasis, an internal balance.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents the net equation for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation shows that six molecules of carbon dioxide and six molecules of water, using light energy, produce one molecule of glucose and six molecules of oxygen.

questions.stem: The text emphasizes that the three components of culture (technological, sociological, ideological) are:

options.B: An integral part of a whole, functioning interdependently.
options.C: Hierarchical, with one being superior to others.

questions.explanation: The document states: 'On the contrary, the three are an integral part of a whole. This is perhaps one of the reasons why culture is sometimes defined as an integrated system of learned behavioural patterns characteristic of the members of a society.'

questions.stem: is the site of synthesis of transfer RNA, ribosomal RNA and ribosomal subunits: a. euchromatin b. heterochromatin c. nucleolus d. golgi body
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a specialized region within the nucleus where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is transcribed, processed, and assembled with proteins to form ribosomal subunits. tRNA synthesis occurs elsewhere in the nucleus. The Golgi body modifies and packages proteins.

questions.stem: __________ ER is a site for lipid and steroid synthesis.
questions.explanation: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid synthesis, detoxification, and calcium ion storage.

questions.stem: Unicellular eukaryotes are grouped into: a. monera b. fungi c. protista d. protista and fungi
questions.explanation: Unicellular eukaryotes, which have a nucleus but are single-celled, are primarily placed in the kingdom Protista. Fungi, while some are unicellular (yeasts), are mostly multicellular.

questions.stem: A cultivated plant type is: a. Eugenia uniflora b. Arachis hypogea c. Vigna unguiculata cv-gr unguiculata d. Coreopsis gigantia
questions.explanation: The abbreviation 'cv' stands for cultivar, which denotes a cultivated plant type. 'gr' likely stands for 'group'. So, 'Vigna unguiculata cv-gr unguiculata' indicates a cultivated variety or group of the species.

questions.stem: One of the major functions of culture is that it gives what to our existence?
questions.explanation: The text states: 'Thus, one of the major functions of culture is that it gives order, meaning and identity to our existence.'

questions.stem: A key gene on the Y chromosome is the __________-determining factor (TDF).
questions.explanation: The Testis-Determining Factor (TDF) gene, usually SRY, triggers male development.

questions.stem: Colchicine is a chemical that stops chromatids from separating during mitosis. Which phase will the cell reach and then stop dividing? A. anaphase B. interphase C. metaphase D. telophase
questions.explanation: Colchicine works by interfering with microtubule polymerization, thus disrupting the spindle apparatus. Since the signal for chromatid separation (anaphase) depends on spindle function, the cell arrests in metaphase, unable to transition to anaphase because the chromatids cannot be pulled apart.

questions.stem: The study of the types or forms of interrelationships among a community of organisms within the same habitat is referred to as: A. autecology B. synecology C. ecology D. ecosystem
questions.explanation: Synecology is the study of groups of organisms (communities) associated together as a unit, focusing on the interactions between different species within a community.

questions.stem: Which of the following occurs during mitosis but not during meiosis I? a. Crossing over b. Reduction to diploid number of chromosomes to haploid c. The nuclear envelopes breaks down d. Separation of sister chromatids

options.B: Reduction to diploid number of chromosomes to haploid

questions.explanation: Sister chromatids separate during anaphase of mitosis and during anaphase II of meiosis, but they do NOT separate during meiosis I (homologous chromosomes separate in anaphase I). Nuclear envelope breakdown occurs in both. Crossing over and reduction to haploid are specific to meiosis I.

questions.stem: What is the primary source of energy for almost all ecosystems?
questions.explanation: Solar energy captured by producers through photosynthesis is the foundational energy input for nearly all ecosystems on Earth.

questions.stem: Storage of polysaccharide in animals.
questions.explanation: Glycogen is the primary storage polysaccharide in animals. It is stored mainly in the liver and muscles. Starch is the storage polysaccharide in plants, cellulose is a structural polysaccharide in plants, and chitin is a structural polysaccharide in fungi and arthropods.

questions.stem: Which structure is primarily responsible for the nourishment of the embryo in placental mammals?
questions.explanation: The placenta is the specialized organ that facilitates nutrient uptake, waste elimination, and gas exchange between maternal and fetal bloodstreams.

questions.stem: Which of the following functions does active transport perform in a cell? a. Packaging proteins for export from the cell b. Distributing enzymes throughout the cytoplasm c.
